dz.headline: Dollar climbs to 136.84 dinars officially as parallel rate nears 250
dz.dek: The US currency rose in both Algerian markets over 10 days, while the euro fell officially and held steady on the parallel market.
paragraphs: The US dollar rose against Algeria’s dinar in both the official and parallel markets, reaching 136.84 dinars on the official market on Tuesday 17 November and 247.5 dinars at Algiers’ Port-Saïd exchange square.

The official rate has risen in recent days and is now a few centimes below 137 dinars, with the dollar approaching the psychological threshold of 140 dinars. On the parallel market, the rate is closing in on 250 dinars, up two dinars in 10 days.

The euro moved the other way on the official market, falling to 150.78 dinars on Tuesday, while it stayed at 276 dinars on the parallel market. The report links the narrowing gap between the euro and dollar to international markets, where they traded between 1.09 and 1.1 dollars per euro, and the dollar is at its highest level since May 2025, supported mainly by expectations on US Federal Reserve interest rates.

dz.headline: Togo leads Algeria 3-0 at half-time in CAN 2027 qualifier
dz.dek: Klidje scored twice and Boateng added a third in Lomé, leaving Algeria's hopes of securing qualification on Tuesday under pressure.
paragraphs: Togo led Algeria 3-0 at half-time on Tuesday, 17 November, in Lomé, in the fourth round of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. Klidje scored in the 18th and 32nd minutes, and Boateng headed Togo's third before the break.

TSA Algerie reported that Algeria fielded a heavily changed side and struggled to threaten, while Togo nearly scored a fourth before half-time. Coach Brahim Hemdani was left to rally his team after the three goals.

Algeria had been in a position to secure qualification on Tuesday, the report said. It suggested Hemdani could bring on more experienced attackers Amine Gouiri, Mohamed Amoura and Fares Chaibi; the report did not give the final score.

dz.headline: Yousef Rabhi wins Ann Arbor mayoral race with 97% of votes
dz.dek: The 38-year-old Democrat, of Algerian origin, will lead the Michigan university city for four years, taking office on 1 December.
paragraphs: Yousef Rabhi, a 38-year-old Democrat of Algerian origin, won Ann Arbor’s mayoral election with 97% of votes counted across 41 polling stations. He will lead the Michigan university city for four years.

No opponent appeared against Rabhi on the official ballot; Elizabeth Kurtz, an activist from homeless communities, ran a write-in campaign. His win followed an August 4 Democratic primary in which he defeated Christopher Taylor, who had led the city for 12 years.

Rabhi’s term begins at noon on 1 December under a revised Michigan election code that delays the start of local mandates. Three newly elected city councillors are also due to take office on that date.

ao.headline: Angola has 370 mil people living with HIV, with fewer than half treated
ao.dek: ANASO president António Coelho said 60% of Angolans living with HIV are aged 15 to 24, and that government struggles to get medicines to those who need them, with stigma.
paragraphs: Angola has 370 mil people living with HIV, and only half receive antiretroviral therapy, ANASO president António Coelho said at the national HIV/AIDS forum. He said 60% of those living with HIV are aged 15 to 24.

Coelho said the government faces serious difficulties making medicines available to people who need them. He also criticised the national commission on HIV/AIDS, saying it operates timidly, and said stigma and discrimination deter many people from seeking treatment.
The report said fewer than 50% of people living with HIV benefit from antiretroviral treatment. Coelho warned that the situation could become alarming without action.

ao.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers through consortium bid
ao.dek: The Global Diamond Consortium is positioned to buy Anglo American’s 85% holding, but Angola has not disclosed its planned investment or financing.
paragraphs: Angola plans to acquire a 10% stake in De Beers through the Global Diamond Consortium, which is positioned to buy Anglo American’s 85% holding in the diamond producer. The Ministry of Mineral Resources, Petroleum and Gas confirmed the plan to Bloomberg.

The consortium, led by former De Beers chief executive Gareth Penny, met Minister Diamantino Azevedo in Luanda on Thursday to present its purchase proposal. The ministry has not said how much Angola plans to invest or how it would finance the deal.

The consortium also includes Namibia, Gulf investors and some of De Beers’ largest customers. If the deal is completed, Angola and Namibia would join Botswana as African shareholders; Botswana’s President Duma Boko announced the country would double its stake to 30%. Anglo American has been trying to sell De Beers since 2024.

ao.headline: PWN Luanda brings women leaders together for 28 November event
ao.dek: The fifth annual meeting at Luanda’s public administration school will discuss women’s leadership and barriers to senior roles.
paragraphs: Professional Women’s Network (PWN) Luanda will hold its fifth annual event on 28 November at the National School of Administration and Public Policy auditorium in Luanda. Professionals from several sectors are due to discuss women’s leadership and their role in changing organisations and society.

The programme includes experience-sharing sessions, debates and networking focused on women’s career obstacles and access to leadership positions. The organisation says it wants to bring professionals from different sectors together and encourage equal opportunities through collaborative learning and stronger support networks.

PWN Luanda, a non-profit formed in 2022, is part of an international network present in about 30 cities. At a Luanda conference in February, Banco de Fomento Angola executive director Francisca Costa said 24% of women had bank accounts and 59% had no formal contact with the financial sector.

ao.headline: Angola dance company turns Cokwe sand drawings into SONA 137
ao.dek: The contemporary work at Luanda’s Teatro Elinga brings geometric designs, traditional sound and movement together on stage.
paragraphs: The Contemporary Dance Company of Angola presented SONA 137, a contemporary dance work, at Teatro Elinga in Luanda about a month before Vanda Narciso wrote about it. The performance draws on sona, geometric sand drawings practised by the Cokwe people, especially in eastern Angola.

Narciso describes the choreography by Ana Clara Guerra Marques and Andy Rodríguez as exploring lines, paths and repeated movements. The original music by David López Sáez combines traditional references, including the kisanji, with contemporary elements. In sona tradition, drawings can carry stories, proverbs and lessons passed between generations.

Founded in 1991, the company is celebrating 35 years in 2026. SONA 137 brings that ancestral tradition into a contemporary performance, with dancers using their bodies to evoke the drawings’ lines and the human relationships they can represent.

bj.headline: Wadagni and To Lam target rice, cashew and cotton trade
bj.dek: The Benin and Vietnam presidents discussed agricultural cooperation, port links and conditions for Vietnamese investment at a meeting in Phnom Penh.
paragraphs: Benin’s President Romuald Wadagni and Vietnam’s President Tô Lâm discussed expanding trade in rice, cashew and cotton at a meeting in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, on 15 November 2026. They also identified freshwater aquaculture as a possible area for cooperation.

The talks covered putting an agricultural cooperation memorandum into effect, with both leaders seeking practical work between businesses in the two countries. They also discussed links between their ports to facilitate commercial exchanges.

Tô Lâm asked Benin’s authorities to create favourable conditions for Vietnamese companies to establish themselves and carry out economic projects in Benin. The presidents also discussed political ties and coordination in international organisations.

bj.headline: Benin’s IAJP urges leaders to put living conditions at the centre of policy
bj.dek: The institute’s four recommendations call for fairer public resource management, stronger essential services and job-focused education.
paragraphs: Benin’s Institute of Artisans of Justice and Peace (IAJP/CO) issued four main recommendations after its 29th annual symposium, held with the Konrad Adenauer Foundation on 13 and 14 November 2026. The institute urged political leaders, economic actors and citizens to make human dignity central to development policy.

In a public appeal released on 14 November, IAJP director Father Arnaud Éric Aguénounon said economic growth and infrastructure projects do not necessarily improve living conditions, particularly in rural areas and urban peripheries. The institute called for greater attention to purchasing power, social justice and access to drinking water, electricity, food and basic health care.

The recommendations also urge more funding for health, education and social protection, fairer distribution of public resources and transparent communication on public works, mining contracts and job opportunities. IAJP called for education reform, vocational training and greater recognition of technical education, manual work and crafts.

bj.headline: Benin qualifies for 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after Burkina Faso win
bj.dek: Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1 in Nouakchott on Tuesday, securing the Guépards a place without playing.
paragraphs: Benin qualified for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on Tuesday, 17 November, without playing, after Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1 in Nouakchott. The result also sent Burkina Faso through to the finals, which will be held in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July 2027.

Benin have 10 points after four rounds, with three wins and one draw. They drew 1-1 with Burkina Faso, beat Mauritania 2-1 and defeated Central African Republic 4-1 in Abidjan on 12 November. Central African Republic lost 1-0 on Monday, with Joseph Ede Oloko scoring in the 93rd minute.

Benin have two matches remaining in March 2027 and are targeting an unbeaten qualifying campaign. It will be the country’s sixth appearance at the tournament and its second consecutive qualification, following the 2008 and 2010 editions. Coach Gernot Rohr’s contract expires on 31 December; he said he had held no discussions about his future.

bj.headline: Benin receives 81 million CFA francs in court equipment
bj.dek: The United States funded the equipment, while the United Nations Development Programme provided technical support for the justice project.
paragraphs: Benin’s Ministry of Justice and Legislation received information technology and audiovisual equipment worth 81 million F Cfa at the Tour administrative on Friday 6 November 2026. The donation was made through the Project to Strengthen Access to Justice, backed financially by the United States and technically by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

The equipment includes 130 digital cameras, 23 laptops, four all-in-one computers, five 65-inch display screens, two 85-inch monitoring screens and a colour multifunction photocopier. The project has total funding of 2.3 million US dollars, Ambassador Peter W. Lord said. It is intended to modernise courts in northern Benin and speed up the handling of cases.

Justice Minister Yvon Détchénou said the equipment would help secure data, preserve evidence, improve services for court users and strengthen internal controls. The delivery completes the project’s planned equipment donations, following vehicles handed over in July 2025; ministry officials were told to use the new items carefully.

bj.headline: FeRCAB opens Parakou production studio for 56 community radios
bj.dek: The shared facility, delivered with Fondation Hirondelle and European Union funding, is intended to help members produce radio and digital content.
paragraphs: Benin’s Federation of Community and Related Radios (FeRCAB) opened a production studio at its headquarters in Parakou on 12 November 2026 for its 56 member stations. Named for federation pioneer Dr Lazare Maurice Sèhouéto, the facility strengthens FeRCAB’s training and co-production centre.

FeRCAB president Dr Inoussa Guinin Asso said the studio would be shared by member stations. He pledged to maintain it, set fair access rules and generate federation income through production services. Fondation Hirondelle partnered on the project, with European Union funding through CFI-Sawara.

The studio is designed to support higher-quality radio and digital productions, including verified and inclusive content. Fondation Hirondelle representative Olympe Dossa said the project would improve community media production conditions; the media regulator, HAAC, called for greater quality in information.

bw.headline: BIDPA says Botswana budget is only moderately geared toward jobs
bw.dek: The policy institute says lasting employment depends on private-sector hiring, while unemployment stands at 27.6 per cent.
paragraphs: Botswana’s 2026/27 budget is only “moderately” employment-oriented, according to a policy brief by the Botswana Institute for Development Policy Analysis (BIDPA). Researchers Masedi Motswapong and Lillian Mookodi say the budget’s ability to sustain jobs depends on whether public spending can lead to durable, privately financed employment.

The country’s labour force has reached roughly 1.17 million, while unemployment rose to 27.6 per cent from 25.9 per cent in 2023. The brief counts 287,060 people actively seeking work; including 76,418 discouraged people who have stopped looking lifts the extended unemployment rate to 32.5 per cent.

Youth unemployment reached 34.4 per cent in 2023 for people aged 15–35, and the rate for those aged 15–24 is estimated at 40–44 per cent. Nearly 41.3 per cent of young people are not in education, employment or training, the brief says.

bw.headline: Botswana's Financial Stability Council says banking system remains resilient
bw.dek: The council warns that the calm in the financial system is not self-sustaining and depends on continued supervision and safe banks.
paragraphs: Botswana's Financial Stability Council concluded on 11 November in Gaborone that the country's financial system remains resilient and supports economic activity. The council based its verdict on the safety and soundness of banks and non-bank financial institutions, the strength of market infrastructures and supervisory arrangements that regulators now describe as effective.

The council's assessment rests on concrete evidence rather than sentiment, according to the report published by the Weekend Post. Its message was carefully hedged: the stability it found is not self-sustaining and requires continued vigilance from regulators and institutions alike, as the broader financial environment grows more uncertain.
The full assessment is available to subscribers only, so further detail on specific measures, figures or next steps is not available in this report.

bw.headline: Gobotswang challenges PEEPA-led Land Board recruitment in court
bw.dek: The Tswapong South MP says the process lacks legal authority over tribal land administration.
paragraphs: Tswapong South MP and Botswana Congress Party (BCP) Shadow Minister for Lands and Agriculture Kesitegile Gobotswang has filed an urgent application at the Gaborone High Court challenging the government's recruitment of Land Board members. The process, led by the Public Enterprises Evaluation and Privatisation Agency (PEEPA), offered three-year appointments to national and local "Land Governance" structures.

In an affidavit sworn on 28 October 2026, Gobotswang argues the recruitment bypasses the Tribal Land Act of 2018 and that PEEPA lacks authority to appoint members who administer tribal land. The exercise began weeks before Land Board members' terms were due to expire in November and closed without an explanation of its legal basis, he says. He also says the criteria give too little weight to the knowledge of local farmers and community members.

Gobotswang says he asked the Lands Minister on 11 October to explain PEEPA's role and called for the process to be suspended, but received no response by his 14 October deadline. He asks the court to treat the silence as evidence that the government cannot justify the exercise. He warns that appointments made through the process could expose land allocations, grants and title cancellations to legal challenge.

bw.headline: Aterian identifies four copper-silver targets in Botswana
bw.dek: The targets lie along a 20-kilometre corridor in the Kalahari Copper Belt, where the company plans more surveys before choosing drilling sites.
paragraphs: London-listed exploration company Aterian has identified four priority copper-silver targets across a 20-kilometre corridor at prospecting licence PL199/2025 in Botswana’s Kalahari Copper Belt. Drone-based magnetic surveys and three-dimensional geophysical interpretation helped identify geological structures the company considers favourable for mineralisation.

Aterian said it has not confirmed mineralisation. Its geological modelling places possible fold structures 10 to 200 metres underground in rocks believed to belong to the D’Kar Formation. Executive chairperson Charles Bray said the four targets give the company several prospects to investigate.

Aterian is preparing induced polarisation and resistivity surveys to better define the structures and rank areas for drilling. The exploration programme is fully funded by the company’s artificial intelligence joint venture with Lithosquare; survey results will guide the selection of drilling targets.

bf.headline: Coris Foundation gives agricultural VDPs 360 tricycles
bf.dek: The 500 million FCFA donation is intended to help the volunteers travel to fields and move harvests to storage sites.
paragraphs: The Coris Foundation handed 360 tricycles to agricultural Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDPs) at the National Office of Major Projects in Burkina Faso on Tuesday, 17 November 2026. The donation is valued at 500 million FCFA and supports the presidential initiative for agricultural production and food self-sufficiency.

Drissa Bassinga, the beneficiaries’ representative, said the vehicles would ease travel to fields and transport produce to storage sites. The tricycles will be distributed among cooperatives formed after the agricultural VDPs’ training, according to the report.

Emmanuel Sawadogo, president of the Coris Foundation, said the donation responds to the president’s call for support for his initiatives. Inoussa Ouédraogo, technical coordinator of the presidential initiative, welcomed private-sector involvement, saying it helps create jobs for young people.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso trains 55 education workers in inclusive teaching and school safety
bf.dek: The four-day Ouagadougou course covers gender-sensitive teaching, preventing gender-based violence in schools and digital tools.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso has opened a four-day training in Ouagadougou for 55 education-sector workers on gender-sensitive teaching, safe learning environments and classroom technology. The course runs from 17 to 20 November 2026.

Participants from the National Institute for Training Education Personnel, the École normale supérieure and central education ministry bodies are studying gender-based violence prevention in schools alongside digital teaching tools. The initiative is supported by Japan’s government and delivered with the UNESCO International Institute for Capacity Building in Africa.

The course is part of a programme launched in March 2024 that covers Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Mali, Mauritania, Niger and Chad. Félicité Kou-nangue of the African Union’s International Centre for Girls’ and Women’s Education in Africa cited 2024 primary-completion rates of 59.9% for girls and 49.3% for boys.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso chamber visits sugar and flour plants in Banfora
bf.dek: SOSUCO's director asked the chamber to help find partners to modernise its factory and expand the land under cultivation.
paragraphs: A delegation from Burkina Faso's Chamber of Commerce and Industry, led by its president, Roland Achille Sow, visited the SOSUCO sugar company and the MINOFA flour mill in Banfora on Monday 16 November 2026. The visits were part of an industrial tour scheduled in Bobo-Dioulasso and Banfora.

SOSUCO director Djakaridja Hema Ouattara told the delegation the company needed to renovate its factory and increase the area available for cultivation. He asked the chamber to help it find partners to support modernisation. The delegation also discussed the plant's operations, development prospects and difficulties, then toured its sugar-production facilities.

Ouattara said SOSUCO wanted to raise annual sugar production from 20 000 tonnes to about 100 000 tonnes. He said the company employed people in the Tannounyan region and called for collective support to restore its production capacity.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1 to qualify for CAN 2027
bf.dek: Aboubacar Camara, Franck Lassina Traoré and Elohim Kaboré scored in Nouakchott, securing qualification with two group matches left.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1 in Nouakchott on Tuesday, 17 November, to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations with two rounds of group matches remaining. Aboubacar Camara opened the scoring in the 11th minute, and Franck Lassina Traoré made it 2-0 before the break.

Mauritania’s Mohamed Ali Diadié headed a goal in the 75th minute, but substitute Elohim Kaboré restored Burkina Faso’s two-goal lead in the 88th. Coach Amir Abdou’s team has 10 points after four matches and is guaranteed a top-two finish in Group F.

Burkina Faso is second behind Benin, also on 10 points, with Benin ahead on goal difference, +5 to +4. The Etalons are scheduled to visit Benin on 24 March 2027 and host the Central African Republic on 28 March, with a chance to finish top of the group.

bf.headline: Sawadogo becomes Burkina Faso’s first cardiovascular surgery associate professor
bf.dek: The Burkinabè doctor passed three examinations at the CAMES health sciences competition in Bangui, qualifying to train future specialists.
paragraphs: Dr Adama Sawadogo has become Burkina Faso’s first associate professor in cardiovascular surgery after passing the 23rd health sciences aggregation competition of the African and Malagasy Council for Higher Education (CAMES), held in Bangui, Central African Republic.

Sawadogo passed three assessments: a presentation of his scientific work, a lecture testing his teaching ability and a clinical examination. Lefaso.net reported that his new rank will allow him to take a greater role in training and supervising future cardiovascular surgery specialists.

In 2024, Lefaso.net interviewed Sawadogo for a report on care for children with heart conditions at Tengandogo University Hospital. The outlet did not report when he will begin his expanded training role.

bi.headline: Coffee Quality Business buys Bukinanyana coffee and employs 110
bi.dek: Raphaël Yaminyibuka bought a local association and its coffee stock after returning to Burundi in 2023 with 25 million Burundian francs.
paragraphs: Raphaël Yaminyibuka returned to his home hill in Burundi in 2023 with 25 million Burundian francs and bought the Ikawa Umwizero Wacu association as its leaders were liquidating assets. He renamed it Coffee Quality Business and bought the coffee stock producers wanted to sell.

Yaminyibuka says his company commits between 700 and 850 million Burundian francs to coffee purchases during a campaign. He says coffee from Bukinanyana commune accounts for half, or as much as a third, of the commune’s harvest arriving at his business. The company employs 110 people: 60 during the coffee campaign and 50 permanently.

He financed the purchase with a loan from a local microfinance institution. Before returning, he moved to Kenya in 2019 after his father died, worked as a mason in Nairobi and then sold eggs on the street; he says an egg sold for 20 shillings.

bi.headline: Burundi opposition parties name presidential candidates
bi.dek: The APDR filed Gabriel Banzawitonde’s bid without the full 100 million Burundian francs deposit, while the CNL chose Nestor Girukwishaka.
paragraphs: Burundi’s APDR and CNL have named candidates for the presidential election scheduled for 3 May 2027, with incumbent Évariste Ndayishimiye running for the ruling CNDD-FDD. The APDR filed its president Gabriel Banzawitonde’s candidacy with the National Independent Electoral Commission on 16 November, but had not raised the required 100 million Burundian francs deposit.

Banzawitonde told journalists he expected to gather the full amount by 22 November, citing difficulty withdrawing such a large sum from banks at once. The CNL’s congress on Sunday selected party official Nestor Girukwishaka; he said the party judged it important to field a candidate rather than risk being seen as leaving politics.

The report says the main opposition forces had also stayed out of the legislative elections. Banzawitonde said the APDR had more reason to expect victory than in 2020, when it backed the ruling party’s candidate.

cm.headline: MRC asks Cameroon officials to clear election-candidate paperwork
cm.dek: The opposition party says thousands of its members face delays, refusals or demands for payment as they prepare for the 7 February 2027 vote.
paragraphs: Tiriane Balbine Noah, president of Cameroon’s Movement for the Renaissance of Cameroon (MRC), said on 17 November that thousands of its members seeking to contest the 7 February 2027 legislative and municipal elections face obstacles assembling their candidacy files. She said officials have refused or delayed some legally required documents, while some candidates have been asked to pay to legalise papers that should be free.

Noah accused administrative and municipal authorities and other officials of trying to discourage MRC candidates. The party called on Elections Cameroon (Elecam) and the ministers responsible for defence, territorial administration and decentralisation to ensure documents are issued promptly and extracts are provided free. It also asked authorities to extend the filing deadline for candidates refused documents.

The MRC urged affected candidates to document refusals for possible legal action. Noah said the party plans to field candidates nationwide and asked the ruling Cameroon People’s Democratic Movement to compete fairly. The filing deadline was approaching, the report said, without specifying its date.

cm.headline: COSUMAF reports Cameroon’s fund-investment share at 3.463%
cm.dek: The regulator’s June figure is down from 20.8% in February, but its reports contain inconsistencies and do not establish that funds sold Cameroonian debt.
paragraphs: Cameroonian government securities made up 3.463% of investments held by collective investment funds in the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC) on June 30, 2026, according to the Central African Financial Market Supervisory Commission (COSUMAF). Its February bulletin put the share at 20.8%.

The figures do not establish that funds reduced their holdings of Cameroonian debt, Business in Cameroon reported. COSUMAF’s February bulletin valued those holdings at CFA249.38 billion, but its first-half report, published November 14, gave no corresponding value for June.

A comparison of the regulator’s publications found a discrepancy of nearly CFA71 billion between two tables in the latest report. Gabon’s share rose from 39.21% to 39.719%, while the Republic of Congo’s increased from 19.32% to 19.930%.

cm.headline: Cameroon allocates CFAF 550 million to 30 student businesses and 50 incubators
cm.dek: Of the 2026 grants, CFAF 350 million goes to ventures at higher education institutions, and nearly two-thirds of student funding backs food processing and agro-industry.
paragraphs: Two notices released on November 13 by the Ministry of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises, Social Economy and Handicrafts (MINPMEESA) set out how Cameroon will spend CFAF 550 million in grants this year, split between 30 student-led businesses and 50 private business incubators. The money pays capital to chosen student ventures and operating support to accredited incubators.

cm.headline: Aeternum signs $1.91 million in funding deals for Cameroon project developer
cm.dek: The eight agreements relate to its planned acquisition of American Renaissance Minerals, which is involved in the Nkamouna project in eastern Cameroon.
paragraphs: U.S.-based Aeternum Resources signed eight financing agreements worth $1.91 million, about CFA1.14 billion, after September 30, as it continues efforts to acquire American Renaissance Minerals, a company involved in developing the Nkamouna nickel-cobalt-manganese project in eastern Cameroon. The acquisition remains unfinished.

Aeternum disclosed the agreements in quarterly financial statements filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 16. The company said it had received none of the money when it prepared the statements, and will record the financing only after funds arrive.

The agreements use Simple Agreements for Future Equity, which allow investors to receive shares later. Each has a $1.60-per-share conversion price cap following Aeternum’s October 1 reverse stock split; none carries interest or a maturity date. The $1.14 billion CFA figure is a contractual commitment, not cash available to Aeternum.

cm.headline: Cameroonian engineer builds solar-powered clay cooler
cm.dek: Didier Dinamou’s prototype uses porous clay, water and a photovoltaic panel, and its designer says it can cool a room to 25 degrees in 48-degree heat.
paragraphs: Cameroonian engineer Didier Dinamou built a clay air conditioner as his final project at the National Advanced School of Engineering of the University of Maroua. The device uses porous clay, water and a photovoltaic panel to cool a room through evaporation.

A solar panel powers a pump that moves water through tubes, while a fan pushes room air across the wet surfaces. The machine works without a grid connection, compressor or refrigerant gas, and includes a USB charging port and a light. Dinamou told Sciences et Vie it can cool a room to 25 degrees when outdoor temperatures reach 48 degrees.

The system can cost 90 000 CFA francs and received a mark of 18,5/20 for Dinamou’s final project. It won first place among 427 entries in the EDF Pulse Africa competition in March 2024. The article says the device could be used in health centres and is suited to dry Sahelian areas.

cf.headline: Central African justice minister orders prosecution of BRDC
cf.dek: The ministry says the political platform is absent from official party registers and has no authorisation after its 13 November march.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic’s justice ministry has ordered prosecutors to bring a case against the Bloc républicain pour la défense de la Constitution (BRDC), a political platform, after its 13 November march. In a note published on 17 November, the ministry challenged the group’s legal status.

Justice Minister Arnaud Djoubaye Abazène said checks by the territorial administration ministry and other competent services found the BRDC was not listed in official party registers and had no authorisation. He instructed public prosecutors to proceed against the platform.
The march took place in Bangui. The ministry’s note makes no further timetable for the prosecution public.

cf.headline: Russian House chief Dimitri Sytyi claims ignorance of Ndassima gold revenue
cf.dek: Sytyi said on Radio Ndeke Luka on 22 September 2026 that mercenary presence in the Central African Republic was free of charge.
paragraphs: On 22 September 2026, Dimitri Sytyi, who runs the Russian House in Bangui, told Radio Ndeke Luka that Russia's support for the Central African Republic costs the state nothing. Pressed on the cost of the mercenary presence and on the mining of national resources, he said the work was free and claimed to know nothing of the revenue from the Ndassima gold deposit.

The Corbeau News Centrafrique report argues that Sytyi's role does not match his claims. The Russian House is a civil, cultural and social institution concerned with education, cooperation and the economy, not the Russian defence ministry or a military headquarters. Yet the report says Sytyi described deployments at Amdafock, the chain of command and security strategy in detail.

The report says he was fluent in military operations but claimed ignorance when questioned about economic activity, which it says should be central to a civil mission. The source gives no official response to the allegations.

cf.headline: Former Central African Republic prime minister Nicolas Tiangaye dies at 70
cf.dek: The lawyer and opposition figure died in Bangui on 16 November after a sudden illness, leaving a decades-long record in law and politics.
paragraphs: Nicolas Tiangaye, a former prime minister of the Central African Republic and former head of its lawyers’ association, died in Bangui on 16 November 2026 at age 70. Radio Ndeke Luka reported that he died after a sudden illness.

Tiangaye became prime minister in January 2013, appointed by President François Bozizé and retained after Bozizé was ousted in March. He resigned on 10 January 2014 alongside transitional leader Michel Djotodia. He also chaired the National Transitional Council in 2003, which helped shape the political transition and constitution.

In the early 1990s, Tiangaye helped establish the Central African Human Rights League and later founded the Republican Convention for Social Progress party. He had recently been active in the Republican Bloc for the Defence of the Constitution. Former transitional head Ferdinand Alexandre N’Guendet, described as his political ally since 2003, called on Central Africans to continue Tiangaye’s work for democracy.

cf.headline: ANAC equips Bangui-M’Poko airport and trains more than 70 staff
cf.dek: The Central African aviation authority handed out certificates and security equipment at the airport on Thursday 12 November, with funding from the African Development Bank.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic’s National Civil Aviation Authority (ANAC) trained more than 70 airport security staff at Bangui-M’Poko and gave them completion certificates on Thursday 12 November. The ceremony also included the handover of equipment to strengthen security at the airport.

The African Development Bank supplied security and screening equipment, sanitary equipment and logistical and office materials, funded at 126 470 800 FCFA. ANAC and the French embassy carried out the training; the embassy said it wants the international airport to meet international standards.

The training is intended to prevent children from entering aircraft parked on the tarmac, after one child was found in an aircraft there on two occasions recently. The work is part of two African Development Bank-funded projects to modernise the airport and support ANAC.

cf.headline: Bangui festival closes after three days of Central African-Chinese arts
cf.dek: The event ran from 9 to 11 November under the arts ministry and the Chinese embassy, featuring performances, photography and martial arts.
paragraphs: A festival showcasing cultural and artistic exchanges between the Central African Republic and China ended on 11 November at a stadium in Bangui, after three days of activities. The event ran from 9 to 11 November under the slogan “Culture, friendship and cooperation between peoples.”

Michel Bamale Bongo, chief of staff at the Ministry of Arts, Culture and Tourism, presided over the closing ceremony. He said participants experienced dance, performances, photography, visual arts and an exhibition of Chinese martial arts. Zhang Wei, chargé d’affaires at China’s embassy in Bangui, said the festival offered an opportunity to share Chinese traditions and discover Central African culture.

Brice Talingano, a participant, said it was the first time photographers had been honoured at such an event. The festival was organised under the arts ministry in partnership with China’s embassy in Bangui.

km.headline: Comorian researcher Faïdat Mzé Hamadi defends doctoral thesis on legume foods in Nantes
km.dek: Her thesis examined how the structure of legume-based model foods relates to their properties and the processes used to make them.
paragraphs: Faïdat Mzé Hamadi, from Moroni, defended her doctoral thesis in Nantes on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, completing research on foods made from legumes.

The thesis, titled Détermination des relations entre structures, propriétés et procédés d'aliment-modèle à base de légumineuses, was carried out at the BIA unit of France's National Research Institute for Agriculture, Food and the Environment (INRAE) in Nantes, in partnership with the GRAPPE unit of the Higher School of Agriculture (ESA) in Angers.
The thesis was supervised by Guy Della Valle, with Sophie Le Gall and Marie Dufrechou as co-supervisors. A jury of several specialists heard the defence.

cg.headline: Congo holds aquaculture forum as local fish output falls short of demand
cg.dek: The country needs about 163 000 tonnes of fish a year, while local production reaches nearly 60 000 tonnes, leaving a gap of more than 100 000 tonnes.
paragraphs: The Republic of Congo held its first Forum on Investment in Aquaculture at the Grande foire agricole du Congo in Bambou Mingali, Ignié district, over the weekend. National fish needs are estimated at about 163 000 tonnes a year, while local production is nearly 60 000 tonnes.

The shortfall of more than 100 000 tonnes is met through imports, Journal de Brazza reported. Nearly 120 experts and sector participants gathered for two days to discuss barriers to aquaculture growth and hear findings from an international organisation’s study of the country’s aquaculture potential.

The forum received financial support from the World Bank and Proclimat and was organised ahead of the planned launch of the Congo Agriculture and Aquaculture Development Project. The initiative is intended to attract investment and increase production capacity.

cg.headline: Fire damages shops and stalls at Dolisie Grand Market
cg.dek: The blaze spread through part of the market near the MUCODEC roundabout on Monday evening, prompting firefighters to call in reinforcements.
paragraphs: A fire broke out on the evening of Monday 16 November in part of the Grand Market in Dolisie, near the MUCODEC roundabout, and spread to several shops and stalls. The flames caused material damage, but the extent of the losses has not been established.

Firefighters responded to contain the blaze and stop it spreading to other businesses. Witness accounts shared on social media said the first fire truck to arrive had no water, complicating the initial response; reinforcements were later mobilised to extinguish the fire. Some traders tried to move their goods to safety as panic spread among merchants and nearby residents.

The cause of the fire remains unknown, and no official account of property losses or casualties has been released. Several traders may have lost a substantial share of their goods and property, according to Journal de Brazza.

cg.headline: Congo loses to Comoros as Claude Le Roy announces resignation
cg.dek: The 1-0 defeat in Brazzaville leaves the national team last in Group G with two points after four matches in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.
paragraphs: Congo lost 1-0 to Comoros in Brazzaville on Tuesday, 17 November, in the fourth round of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. Ben Chayeel Hamada scored the only goal in the 32nd minute.

After the defeat, Congo coach Claude Le Roy said he intended to resign, saying he had failed in his task. Congo have two points from four Group G matches, with one goal scored and three conceded; second-placed Comoros have seven points.
Congo drew 0-0 away to Comoros in Moroni on 13 November. The team has two qualifying matches left, and Le Roy said a miracle would be needed for Congo to reach the finals.

cg.headline: Congo Terminal installs simulator to train port-equipment operators
cg.dek: The 3D system lets workers practise emergencies without taking cranes, terminal vehicles or tugboats out of service.
paragraphs: Congo Terminal received and put into operation a 3D training simulator on 13 November at its Operations Directorate. The equipment recreates conditions for using STS gantry cranes, RTG cranes, mobile cranes and port tugboats.

The company said the simulator lets operators practise routine work and rare emergencies without tying up the terminal’s working equipment. Training manager Ngala Sanda said it is expected to cut training hours by 30 to 40 % and let experienced operators refresh their skills more often, at lower cost.

Technical director Kehindé Salami said the system allows teams to repeat varied exercises without interrupting operations. Congo Terminal said the simulator is also intended to support training across the AGL network and ports of medium size.

cg.headline: Congo presents three priorities at Francophonie meeting in Phnom Penh
cg.dek: Foreign Minister Constant Serge Bounda urged member states to back a forest decade, Kébé-Kébé heritage status and Congo’s bid for a UN Security Council seat.
paragraphs: The Republic of Congo presented three priorities for member-state support at the 48th Ministerial Conference of La Francophonie in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, on 14 November. Foreign Minister Constant Serge Bounda, who led the Congolese delegation, called for the Francophone community to support the United Nations Decade for Afforestation and Reforestation, covering 2027-2036.

Brazzaville also sought backing for Kébé-Kébé’s nomination to UNESCO’s list of intangible cultural heritage. Its third priority is a bid for a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council for 2030-2031; Congo cited its experience in mediation and seeking political solutions to crises.

The ministerial session finalised strategic documents for heads of state and government, who met in Phnom Penh on 15 and 16 November. The gathering also addressed the designation of the organisation’s next secretary-general.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast says African energy bank will start on Jan. 2 in Abuja
ci.dek: Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly said the APPO and Afreximbank project will mobilise funding for Africa’s energy sector and infrastructure.
paragraphs: Ivory Coast’s mines, petroleum and energy minister, Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, said the African Energy Bank will begin operations on Jan. 2, 2027, in Abuja, Nigeria. He announced the date on Tuesday, Nov. 17, in Abidjan, at the opening of the African Petroleum Producers’ Organization’s 50th ministerial session.

The bank is a joint project of the African Petroleum Producers’ Organization (APPO) and the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank). Sangafowa-Coulibaly said its first general assembly was held in Nigeria on Oct. 31, electing directors and appointing the institution’s first president and auditor. He described the bank as a way to mobilise financing for energy development amid limited access to capital and infrastructure needs.

The session is also considering APPO’s 2026 budget execution and proposed 2027 budget, its long-term strategy and nominations to the organisation’s bodies for 2027. The bank’s planned launch follows the assembly’s appointments.

ci.headline: Prosecutor seeks five years in prison for Blaise Lasm
ci.dek: The Ivory Coast opposition figure is charged with plotting against state authority, but prosecutors could not date videos presented at trial.
paragraphs: Prosecutors in Abidjan on Monday 16 November requested five years in prison for Blaise Lasm, a senior figure in Laurent Gbagbo’s PPA-CI party, on a charge of plotting against state authority without an act. The court is due to deliver its ruling on 30 November.

The prosecution presented videos at trial but could not establish when they were recorded, Afrique Sur 7 reported. Lasm’s lawyer said the defence had not received the footage during the investigation or instruction. Lasm said one video was recorded in 2019 or 2020, rather than between August and September 2025, as prosecutors argued.

A September 7, 2026 order had already dropped charges of inciting insurrection and undermining territorial integrity, leaving the charge on which Lasm is being tried. Prosecutors also requested five years’ loss of civic rights and a five-year ban on leaving his home department. Three years in prison were sought for fellow PPA-CI deputy secretary-general Dahi Nestor Douhouré.

ci.dek: The operation at M’Basso in Tengréla department was carried out at dawn on Monday, 16 November, as surveillance of areas exposed to illegal mining was stepped up.
paragraphs: A detachment of Ivory Coast’s Special Surveillance and Intervention Brigade (BSSI) destroyed 18 dredges used for illegal gold mining on the Bagoué River, near M’Basso in Tengréla department, on Monday, 16 November. The operation began at dawn.

ci.headline: Dehima Mission holds peace prayer in Tiassalé
ci.dek: The ceremony on 15 November formed part of the 31st annual peace celebrations organised by the AD3T association in the town.
paragraphs: The Dehima Mission held a prayer for peace at Tiassalé town hall on 15 November, as part of Côte d’Ivoire’s National Peace Day. The ceremony was initiated by Anouanzè Dehima of Tiassalé, Taabo and Toumodi, known as AD3T.

Mermoz Koffi, the event’s organising committee president, said the mission had maintained a tradition of peace prayers since 1988. Preacher Oka Kouadio urged worshippers and Ivorians to practise forgiveness and tolerance in daily life. Tiassalé Mayor Assalé Tiémoko, also a mission member, called on residents to adopt peaceful attitudes.

The AD3T celebrations ran from 13 to 15 November and marked their 31st edition. They also recognised 50 years of priesthood for Etien Koffi Mathieu, the Dehima national council president and AD3T founder. Koffi said the mission prayed for peace before the national observance was established by decree in 1996.

eg.headline: Egyptian phone output and exports could help lower prices, commerce official says
eg.dek: Walid Ramadan said imported components, including RAM, raise costs, while Egypt’s market needs about 20 million phones a year.
paragraphs: Walid Ramadan, vice chairman of the Mobile and Telecommunications Division at the Cairo Chamber of Commerce, said on Monday that higher local production and exports could help reduce mobile phone prices in Egypt. He said the domestic market requires about 20 million phones annually.

Ramadan told the al-Hekaya phone-in programme that most phone components are imported and shortages of parts such as RAM can push prices up. Larger production runs would spread costs across more units, helping manufacturers pass the break-even point and lower unit costs, he said.

He urged the Ministry of Industry and Trade to meet manufacturers about production-cost barriers. Ramadan also proposed energy-cost relief, tax breaks or export rebates, and said exports to countries with which Egypt has trade agreements could help expand output.

eg.headline: Egypt calls for permanent Nile intelligence centre and legal track
eg.dek: Water Minister Hani Sewilam says Ethiopia’s dam operations require notification, data sharing and coordination during droughts and floods.
paragraphs: Egypt is urging a shift in how it manages the Nile dispute with Ethiopia, calling for a permanent centre to assess the basin and the Horn of Africa and a sustained legal and technical effort over damage from unilateral dam operations. The proposals are set out in an Egypt Independent commentary published on 17 November.

The commentary says Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam has adopted a more direct public position on the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. It says Egypt accepts Ethiopia’s right to development but rejects unilateral control over a shared watercourse, and says Ethiopia remains bound by duties to notify downstream countries, share data and coordinate during droughts and floods.

A newly announced Egyptian-Sudanese committee is tasked with assessing the effects of unilateral operation and pursuing compensation, the commentary says. It also urges Egypt to engage international banks, sovereign funds and engineering firms before new dams are built, and to develop regional economic projects.

eg.headline: Misr Life Insurance to offer 15% stake on EGX in December
eg.dek: The sale covers 750 million existing shares held by state-owned Misr Insurance Holding, with the price set through a bookbuilding process.
paragraphs: Misr Life Insurance plans to sell 15% of its shares on the Egyptian Exchange, with subscriptions and trading expected to begin in December 2026. The proposed initial public offering comprises 750 million existing ordinary shares held by Misr Insurance Holding Company, which is wholly owned by the Sovereign Fund of Egypt for Investment and Development.

The offer will include a private placement for qualified investors in Egypt and selected jurisdictions outside the United States, plus a public offer open to investors in Egypt. Both portions will have the same per-share price, set through bookbuilding. The selling shareholder’s remaining shares will be subject to lock-up restrictions under exchange rules and customary market practice.

Misr Life Insurance is seeking approvals from the Financial Regulatory Authority, including approval of the prospectus and registration of the shares, as well as approvals from the exchange. The December timetable depends on regulatory clearance and market conditions. EFG Hermes is the sole global coordinator and bookrunner.

eg.headline: Egypt seeks Ramsar funding to restore Lake Qarun wetlands
eg.dek: Environment Minister Manal Awad raised funding with Ramsar chief Musonda Mumba to tackle pollution and improve the lake’s ecological condition.
paragraphs: Egypt’s Environment Minister Manal Awad discussed securing funding to restore wetlands and tackle pollution in Egyptian lakes, with particular focus on Lake Qarun, during talks with Ramsar Convention Secretary-General Musonda Mumba at COP31 in Antalya.

Mumba said the convention’s secretariat was seeking closer cooperation with Turkey, which chairs the Mediterranean Wetlands Working Group, to mobilise money for addressing chemical pollution and improving important lakes. She said Lake Qarun provides habitat for migratory birds and livelihoods and jobs, particularly for fishermen and farmers.

Egypt has four wetlands of international importance under the convention: Lakes Bardawil and Burullus, and the Wadi El-Rayan and Qarun protected areas. The country’s 2024–2030 biodiversity strategy sets 21 national targets, including restoring 20% of degraded ecosystems.

eg.headline: Trevor Noah to close UTH youth festival in Cairo
eg.dek: The two-day event at the Grand Egyptian Museum on 20 and 21 November is built around the theme “Work in Progress.”
paragraphs: UTH, a youth culture platform that produces media, community programmes and events for young Egyptians, will hold its third annual festival at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on 20 and 21 November. Thousands of young people are expected, and comedian Trevor Noah is scheduled to close the weekend in what the organisers say is his first appearance in Egypt.

The festival targets Egyptians aged 18 to 28 who have not yet settled their careers or lives. Its 2026 theme, “Work in Progress”, or taht el-inshaa in Arabic, asks speakers to show drafts, rejections and changes of direction rather than polished success stories.

UTH began as the Youth Summit. Its first edition in 2024 drew more than 2,000 people to the museum, according to the organisers, and the 2025 edition at the American University in Cairo’s New Cairo campus grew to more than 5,000 attendees and over 100 speakers.

gq.headline: CEMAC reviews Malabo proposals to reform its institutions
gq.dek: The Central African bloc is examining governance, funding, staffing and oversight, with deadlines for a mandate-based post review set for December.
paragraphs: The Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa (CEMAC) is reviewing proposals in Malabo to improve governance and financing across its institutions. The sessions bring together institutional officials, experts and representatives of its Technical Secretariat to examine problems in the division of responsibilities, programme delivery and access to resources.

Mbasogo Kung Nguidang, the steering committee’s president, said the discussions should build on issues examined in Malabo from 26 to 28 October and produce practical measures for future reform decisions. The agenda covers governance, finances, human resources, and monitoring and evaluation. The minister said CEMAC institutions depend on effective transfers of the Community Integration Tax to fund budgets and activities, while uncertainty over financing requires a collective response.

A review of posts subject to mandates is to follow its scheduled stages, with deadlines in December. The conclusions will record agreements, reservations and matters needing decisions by competent bodies; recommendations are to be prioritised and assessed for legal feasibility and financial implications. They will inform the next steering committee session.

gq.dek: The agreement sets a basis for future education cooperation after the country proposed training in energy, mining, aviation and digital skills.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea and the Singapore Institute of Technology signed a memorandum of understanding on Tuesday, 17 November, to lay the groundwork for future education cooperation. The signing came during an official visit to Singapore by the country's vice-president.

Simeón Oyono Esono Angué, minister of state for foreign affairs, cooperation and the diaspora, who led the delegation, had proposed the memorandum as a first step towards a fuller agreement. He outlined training needs in oil and gas production, plant maintenance, mining equipment, aircraft piloting and maintenance, and cybersecurity.
The institute said it was willing to share its education and technology experience. It works with about 35 countries and offers more than 40 programmes across five faculties.

gq.headline: Zimbabwe beats Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Group E qualifier
gq.dek: The result leaves Nzalang Nacional under pressure in the race for places at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, after the teams had drawn 0-0.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe beat Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare on Monday in the fourth round of Group E qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. The defeat leaves Equatorial Guinea needing results in its remaining matches to keep its qualification hopes alive.

Thandolwenkosi Ngwenya put the hosts ahead in the fourth minute at the National Sports Stadium. Equatorial Guinea created chances through Cristian Makaté, Santiago Eneme and Rony Mbomio, but Zimbabwe goalkeeper Nelson Chadya made important first-half saves, Ahora EG reported.

Before the match, Equatorial Guinea and Zimbabwe each had four points, while the Democratic Republic of Congo led the group with nine. The sides had drawn 0-0 on the 12th of the month; the tournament’s final stage is scheduled for Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

er.headline: Ethiopian forces push Tigrayan fighters toward Eritrean border
er.dek: Clashes have been reported near Badme as artillery was fired toward dwellings close to the Eritrean border town.
paragraphs: Ethiopian forces have pushed Tigrayan fighters toward Eritrea’s border after renewed clashes in the contested area near Badme, a border town in Eritrea. The Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF), backed by pro-government militia, have advanced into Tigray, northern Ethiopia, against forces allied with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).

ACLED, a conflict-monitoring organization, reports skirmishes at several locations as the ENDF moved the Tigrayan Defense Forces toward the border. The Ethiopian troops also fired heavy artillery toward dwellings near Badme. No casualty figure is given in the report.

The TPLF-allied fighters began their offensive on September 23, seeking to overthrow Ethiopia’s government as part of a rebel coalition. Abdurahman Sayed, director of the London-based Horn of Africa Center for Regional Integration, said Ethiopia might see reclaiming Badme as a way to ease its internal conflict. The town was awarded to Eritrea by a boundary commission after the 1998-2000 war.

ke.headline: Ruto returns to Parliament with Sh5 trillion plan under scrutiny
ke.dek: The National Infrastructure Fund holds Sh310.6 billion in starting capital, against a wider ambition to raise Sh5 trillion over a decade.
paragraphs: President William Ruto addresses Parliament on Wednesday in his 2026 State of the Nation Address, nearly a year after unveiling a Sh5 trillion transformation blueprint. Its four priorities cover people, net exports, water storage and irrigation, and energy and transport.

Kenya's National Treasury, in its Draft 2027 Budget Policy Statement, says the National Infrastructure Fund began with Sh310.6 billion: Sh106.3 billion from the Kenya Pipeline Company share sale and Sh204.3 billion from the partial Safaricom stake sale. Treasury papers show no binding commitments from outside investors at the size the plan needs.

Officials aim to raise up to Sh5 trillion over time, with about US$2 billion in international co-investment sought through certified funds. A High Court ruling nullifying the partial Safaricom sale is under appeal by the State. The World Bank puts gross public debt at 69.9 per cent of GDP at the end of June 2026.

ke.headline: Thugge backs Treasury plan to centralise county deposits at CBK
ke.dek: The proposed law would require counties to get written Treasury approval before opening or closing accounts and move their funds into a single account.
paragraphs: Central Bank of Kenya Governor Kamau Thugge has backed proposed amendments to the Public Finance Management Act that would centralise county government deposits at the central bank. He presented his support to the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Budget in Nairobi on Nov. 18.

The plan would require counties to obtain written approval from the National Treasury before opening or closing bank accounts, and consolidate county funds in a Treasury Single Account at the CBK. Thugge said the changes would improve oversight, reduce commercial bank accounts and lower borrowing costs by giving the Treasury access to idle public funds.

Thugge also proposed limiting each county to one commercial bank imprest account, with main operational and project accounts held at the CBK. He told senators that keeping county deposits at the central bank would avoid interest payments when government resources were already available.

ke.headline: Kenya hosts global parliamentary hunger summit
ke.dek: The 16-17 November meeting brings parliamentarians and development partners together to discuss food security, nutrition and agrifood systems.
paragraphs: Lawmakers, parliamentary networks and development partners from around the world are meeting in Kenya from 16 to 17 November for the 2026 Global Parliamentary Summit Against Hunger and Malnutrition.

The summit is jointly organised by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation and Kenya's Parliament, with other parliamentary partners. Delegates are discussing the right to food, access to healthy diets and resilient, sustainable agrifood systems.

Gender equality, rural communities and access to safe, affordable, nutritious food are also on the agenda. Earlier editions were held in Spain in 2018 and Chile in 2023, and the organisers say the aim is to turn international commitments into action through legislation, oversight and accountability.

ke.headline: Gachagua presses IEBC for a full day of election technology talks
ke.dek: The opposition leader says Thursday’s two-and-a-half-hour meeting is too short to discuss Smartmatic and voter registration ahead of the 2027 polls.
paragraphs: Rigathi Gachagua, leader of the Democracy of the Citizens Party, has asked Kenya’s Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) to extend Thursday’s consultation with opposition leaders to a full day. The talks are to address whether to renew election technology provider Smartmatic’s contract or choose another way to continue voter registration ahead of the 2027 polls.

Gachagua said the scheduled two-and-a-half hours would not give him enough time to present concerns raised by Kenyans. He said he needed at least one and a half hours to address commissioners and had requested a full day for consultation. The IEBC invited opposition principals after Gachagua called over the weekend for political parties and other stakeholders to discuss the technology for the election.

Gachagua also urged the Registrar of Persons to meet opposition leaders over what he alleges is bias in issuing national identity cards. He claimed applicants in areas seen as supporting President William Ruto received IDs in two to three days, while those in opposition strongholds waited up to seven months. He said he would take the matter to the registrar, arguing the delays disadvantage young people as voter registration continues.

ke.dek: The movement plans town halls, community dinners and meetings with elected officials, with Kenyan diaspora communities at the centre, until December 7.
paragraphs: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi Movement has unveiled a United States tour running from November 21 to December 7, with events in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Washington DC, Texas, Washington state and California. The movement said the tour begins with the opening of its office in Hackettstown, New Jersey, at noon on November 21.

According to the movement's itinerary, the team will hold a town hall meeting at The Palace Center in Allentown, Pennsylvania, from 2pm to 6pm on November 22, and a community dinner at Spark Hotel in Maryland on November 23. The tour also includes meetings with Gen Z groups and elected officials, and a Thanksgiving dinner in Dallas on November 27.

The schedule runs through Houston, where a women's caucus is set for November 29, and then Seattle-area events on December 3 and 4. The final listed engagement is a dinner in Silicon Valley on December 7, scheduled to begin at 5pm.

za.headline: Astral Foods holds firm on pay as Festive Chicken strike spreads
za.dek: The poultry group says it cannot meet workers’ demands for increases above 74%, while some employees are seeking more than 100%.
paragraphs: Astral Foods is enforcing “no work, no pay” as employees at its Festive Chicken factory in Olifantsfontein, Gauteng, continue a strike that has spread to workers at some group farms. The strike, led by the Simunye Workers’ Forum (SWF), has lasted more than two weeks.

Astral chief executive Gary Arnold told The Citizen that some factory workers have returned, while others remain on strike. SWF members seek a monthly salary of R13 500, up from R6 500 for the lowest-paid workers. Arnold said the group is still recovering from severe losses caused by load shedding and cannot provide the demanded increase of more than 74%; some workers seek increases above 100%.

Arnold said workers approached the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) over the pay dispute and received a certificate of non-resolution. He said they had no picketing rules and were acting under the Public Gatherings Act. A 2023 change to CCMA rules clarified commissioners’ responsibilities in disputes that could lead to strikes, according to law firm Cliffe Dekker Hofmeyr, which was not commenting on this strike.

za.headline: DA weighs mayoral swap as Johannesburg coalition talks stall
za.dek: The proposal would send party leader Geordin Hill-Lewis to Johannesburg and Helen Zille to Cape Town, but Zille says she is not taking it seriously.
paragraphs: Helen Zille has dismissed talk of replacing Geordin Hill-Lewis as Cape Town mayor, as reports describe a proposed swap that would make Hill-Lewis Johannesburg mayor. The idea has been raised with ActionSA during coalition negotiations with the Democratic Alliance (DA), according to sources in both parties.

The DA won 91 of Johannesburg’s 270 council seats in the 4 November local government elections, leaving it short of a majority. ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba has said his party will not back Zille for Johannesburg mayor and offered to leave the race if she does. Hill-Lewis told 702 that ActionSA’s demand to drop Zille was difficult for the DA to accept, but he has not ruled out working with the party.

Zille, who was Cape Town mayor from 2006 to 2009 before becoming Western Cape premier, said she was not taking the rumour seriously. She has previously said she would lead the DA’s opposition caucus in Johannesburg if she did not secure the mayoralty; the DA has not announced changes to its mayoral candidates.

za.headline: Weather service warns of flooding and power cuts in two provinces
za.dek: A Yellow Level 2 alert covers severe thunderstorms in parts of the Free State and North West on Wednesday, 18 November.
paragraphs: South Africa's weather service issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms in parts of the Free State and North West on Wednesday, 18 November. The storms are expected to bring localised flooding, property damage and disruptions to power and communication services.

The service said the warning covers northern and northeastern parts of the Free State and southeastern parts of the North West. It forecast isolated to scattered showers and thundershowers in the central and eastern Free State, and isolated showers and thundershowers in eastern North West.

The service forecast extremely high fire danger in western parts of both provinces, as well as the Northern Cape and parts of the Western Cape. Very hot to extremely hot conditions are also expected in the interior of the Namakwa District and along parts of the Western Cape coast and interior.

za.headline: Four Zimbabweans abandon bail bids in South Africa war-recruitment case
za.dek: The fifth accused, Abel Muchenje, plans to seek release, but prosecutors told the Kempton Park court they will oppose his application.
paragraphs: Four of five Zimbabwean nationals accused of trying to leave South Africa to join the Russia-Ukraine war abandoned their bail applications at Kempton Park Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, 17 November. The fifth, Abel Muchenje, 40, said he intends to apply for bail.

National Prosecuting Authority spokesperson Magaboke Mohlatlole said prosecutors would oppose Muchenje’s application. The five were arrested on 8 November after an intelligence-led investigation, while allegedly preparing to board flights out of South Africa. They face charges under the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act 15 of 1998.

The court postponed the case to 24 November for possible plea and sentence negotiations under the Criminal Procedure Act. The four who dropped their applications are Weight Mudhanyane, 23, Javangwe Munyaradzi, 41, Wesley Sothole, 24, and Knowledge Ndunduma, 46.

paragraphs: Netflix will launch the first South African edition of Love Is Blind on 4 December, with 27 single contestants trying to find a spouse without seeing their potential partners. The series is hosted by Dineo and Solo Langa.

Six episodes are scheduled for the opening release, followed by two on 11 December and the final episode on 18 December. Contestants date in specially designed pods, where they can speak through a wall; they must get engaged to progress and meet face to face.
Cape Town production house afrOkaans produces the show. After the pod dates, couples who progress travel to a location where they can spend time together in person and meet the other couples.

paragraphs: Nigeria’s inflation fell for a fourth straight month and the Central Bank began cutting rates as the country’s stock market climbed about 60% for the year, according to Nairametrics on Nov. 17.
The report described Nigeria as entering the final weeks of 2026 in better macroeconomic shape than at any point in three years, while saying conditions beneath the headline gains were mixed.
The report also cited a harvest discount, but gave no details about its size or who was offering it.

ng.headline: AFEX forecasts 1.9 million-tonne fall in Nigeria rice output
ng.dek: The exchange also projects a 1.5 million-tonne decline in maize production during the 2026/2027 market season, based on a survey of about 41,000 farmers.
paragraphs: AFEX Commodities Exchange forecasts Nigeria’s rice production will fall by 1.9 million metric tonnes in the 2026/2027 market season, according to its 2026 Wet Season Crop Production Report. The exchange also projects maize output will decline by 1.5 million metric tonnes.

The report draws on surveys of approximately 41,000 randomly selected farmers nationwide, alongside data from AFEX and other agricultural research bodies. AFEX said improved fertiliser availability during the 2026 wet season was partly linked to subsidy interventions by federal and state governments.

AFEX chief executive Akinyinka Akintunde called for stronger agricultural data systems and reforms to lift production capacity. The exchange said improved access to finance, agricultural infrastructure and targeted interventions were needed to address the projected declines.

ng.headline: Nigeria targets $9.3bn care economy and seeks private investment
ng.dek: The Federal Executive Council approved a 2026–2030 policy, while a proposed bill would give it legislative backing.
paragraphs: Nigeria is targeting a $9.3 billion care economy and seeking private investment in childcare, elderly care and disability support after the Federal Executive Council approved the National Care Policy and Implementation Plan 2026–2030. The policy is intended to organise the sector and expand jobs and women’s participation in the economy.

Women’s Affairs Minister Hajiya Imaan Suleiman-Ibrahim said on Tuesday in Lagos that the council directed the justice and women’s affairs ministers on October 28 to draft an executive bill backing the policy. Citing UN Women’s 2026 modelling, she said closing unpaid care gaps and expanding universal childcare could add at least $9.3 billion to gross domestic product and create 9.4 million to 17 million jobs. Caregiving accounted for 20.16 per cent of women’s withdrawal from the workforce, against 0.6 per cent for men.

International Finance Corporation Nigeria head Christian Mulamula said 92 per cent of childcare facilities were small, independently owned businesses and 76 per cent of childcare entrepreneurs lacked formal finance. Lagos is developing an investment-oriented care policy framework, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu said through his finance commissioner, and urged investors and financial institutions to support the sector.

ng.headline: OPay names five finalists for ₦18m National Innovation Challenge
ng.dek: The Nigerian digital bank says more than 11,000 students took part in selection, training and mentorship for the 2026 competition.
paragraphs: OPay, a Nigerian digital bank, has named five finalist teams for its 2026 National Innovation Challenge, which carries ₦18m in prizes. The competition is run with Google and the Federal Government’s 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT) Programme.

ng.headline: London deletes posts praising Nigeria-US security partnership
ng.dek: The American strategist had called Nigeria Washington’s greatest ally in Africa and said the cooperation could widen economic and trade opportunities.
paragraphs: American political strategist Diana London deleted social media posts praising Nigeria’s security partnership with the United States, according to The Punch’s report on Wednesday. London had described Nigeria as Washington’s greatest ally in Africa and said cooperation under Presidents Bola Tinubu and Donald Trump was producing results.

In posts on X, London credited the two governments with working to tackle terrorism and strengthen bilateral relations. She also said the partnership could open economic and trade opportunities. The Punch’s assigned report says the posts were deleted but gives no reason for their removal.

President Tinubu has also given London an exclusive interview, according to Imran Muhammad, a senior aide to the chairman of the governing All Progressives Congress. Muhammad said the interview was expected to be released soon.

et.headline: IGAD brings 2023 treaty into force, replacing its 1996 agreement
et.dek: The eight-member bloc's new treaty covers 18 areas of cooperation, including trade, free movement of people and agriculture.
paragraphs: The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), a regional organisation of eight states, has brought its 2023 treaty into force. The new treaty replaces the 1996 agreement that gave the bloc its legal framework for nearly three decades. Ethiopia is one of five member states that had ratified it by September 2026.

The IGAD Council of Ministers confirmed on September 15 that the required threshold of two-thirds ratification had been met. IGAD Executive Secretary Workneh Gebeyehu said the agreement would strengthen the region's collective capacity to respond to crises. The treaty covers 18 areas under Article 24, including trade liberalisation, free movement of people and labour, renewable energy, agriculture and food security.

The treaty also clarifies the responsibilities of IGAD institutions, sets more structured mechanisms for resolving disputes and reinforces members' duty to implement decisions. The revision targets gaps in enforcement and dispute procedures under the old agreement. The announcement coincides with IGAD's 40th anniversary; the body was founded in 1986 to coordinate action on drought and food insecurity.

et.headline: Ethiopia opens central bank sandbox for financial firms
et.dek: The framework lets banks, fintechs and insurers test products under National Bank supervision before seeking full approval or wider market entry.
paragraphs: Ethiopia’s National Bank opened a regulatory sandbox on November 17, allowing financial firms to test products, services and technologies in a live, controlled setting before full approval or wider market entry. The framework covers fintechs, commercial banks, insurers and other financial institutions.

Applicants must show that a proposal is innovative, offers consumer benefits and cannot be tested under existing rules. The bank will issue calls for applications at least twice a year, and fees range from 35,000 birr for general applicants to 100,000 birr for commercial banks.

Approved trials can run for up to 12 months, with one extension of another year subject to progress and central bank approval. Participants must follow anti-money laundering, cybersecurity and data-protection laws, and obtain customers’ written consent before enrolling them.

et.headline: Dodai closes $16 million Series A with Tokyo Gas-backed extension
et.dek: The Ethiopian electric-mobility company secured a further $3 million from Tokyo Gas and Singapore-based Kaneto Capital Management.
paragraphs: Ethiopian electric-mobility startup Dodai closed its Series A at $16 million after securing a $3 million extension from Tokyo Gas and Singapore-based family office Kaneto Capital Management. The extension adds to a $13 million round completed earlier this year, comprising $8 million in equity and $5 million in debt.

Tokyo Gas invested through its corporate venture capital subsidiary, Acario, while Kaneto joined as a new institutional backer. Founded in 2021 by Japanese entrepreneur Yuma Sasaki, Dodai designs and assembles electric motorbikes and operates battery-swapping stations for delivery and logistics workers. It has deployed more than 2,000 bikes in Ethiopia, employs more than 150 people, about 98 percent of them Ethiopian, and runs about 10 swapping stations in Addis Ababa.

The company says its active fleet is estimated at about 2,500 bikes. Ethiopia exempts completely knocked-down electric-vehicle kits assembled locally from customs duties, excise taxes and value-added tax; semi-knocked-down kits face a 5 percent tariff. The government has set a target of 500,000 electric vehicles on the road by 2030. Tokyo Gas is expected to advise Dodai on power management and its battery-swapping network.

gh.headline: Cedi’s year-to-date fall against dollar reaches 10.6 per cent
gh.dek: Bank of Ghana data puts the dollar at GH¢11.69 on the interbank market in November, while Fitch Solutions forecasts further weakness in 2027.
paragraphs: The Ghana cedi’s year-to-date depreciation against the US dollar reached 10.6 per cent in November, according to the Bank of Ghana’s latest Summary of Economic and Financial Data. The dollar traded at GH¢11.69 on the interbank market that month.

Fitch Solutions forecasts that the cedi will average GH¢12.40 to the dollar in 2027. Associate Director Mike Kruiniger said lower gold prices and the government’s foreign-exchange reserve accumulation drive could limit dollar flows into the domestic market.

Kruiniger said tighter dollar supply could make it harder for the cedi to withstand demand and bring back price pressures next year. The report says a weaker cedi would raise the cost of imported goods and production inputs, adding pressure to businesses and inflation.

gh.headline: Ghana banks face pressure to make digital services work reliably
gh.dek: The Bank of Ghana reported rising mobile-money transaction values and volumes in the first quarter of 2025 compared with a year earlier.
paragraphs: Ghanaian banks are handling more payments, transfers and account services through digital channels, while customers and businesses increasingly depend on them for everyday transactions. The shift is raising expectations for reliable, secure services that work across payment platforms.

The Bank of Ghana’s 2025 Payment Systems Oversight Annual Report said new technologies, changing customer behaviour and cooperation across the financial sector helped make payment channels more efficient, secure and accessible. Its FinTech Sector Report for the first quarter of 2025 recorded higher mobile-money transaction values and volumes than in the corresponding period of 2024.

Banks are being urged to judge digital services by completed customer journeys, not just how many people start an online process. The measures cited include transaction success rates, service availability, complaint volumes, resolution times and continued customer use; branches and service centres remain important for complex issues and disputed transactions.
