gh.headline: Ghana and US renew cooperation to curb mercury pollution from illegal mining
gh.dek: The partnership will share scientific expertise and technology to improve monitoring and promote mercury-free gold extraction in Ghana.
paragraphs: Ghana and the United States renewed cooperation to tackle mercury pollution from illegal mining at a two-day symposium in Accra, focusing on scientific collaboration, technology transfer and sustainable gold extraction.

US Embassy Chargé d’Affaires Rolf Oslon said contamination threatens freshwater sources including the Pra and Ankobra rivers. He cited mercury levels in the Birim River that exceeded a community water treatment plant’s capacity, affecting its operations.

The symposium was organised through the US Government’s Ambassador’s Water Experts Programme, a joint initiative of the US Departments of the Interior and State. Oslon said the United States supports Ghana’s efforts against illegal mining, including activity financed and undertaken by foreign actors.

gh.headline: Ghana launches 2026-2028 migration strategy to coordinate agencies
gh.dek: Interior Minister Muntaka Mohammed Mubarak says the plan will strengthen migrant protection, border management and action against trafficking and smuggling.
paragraphs: Ghana has launched the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) Strategy for 2026-2028, a plan to coordinate state agencies and strengthen collaboration with society on migration governance. Interior Minister Muntaka Mohammed Mubarak launched the revised strategy with IOM, the Ghana Immigration Service and other state institutions.

Mubarak said the plan would improve systems to identify, refer and protect migrants, support voluntary return and help migrants reintegrate, particularly vulnerable people. He said stronger national referral mechanisms would help ensure vulnerable migrants receive support. The strategy also calls for better migration data, contingency planning and risk monitoring to respond to insecurity, climate vulnerability, displacement and public health emergencies.

IOM Ghana led development of the plan. IOM Chief of Mission Fatou Diallo Ndiaye said the organisation would support Ghana’s efforts and promote policy coordination at national, regional and international levels. By 2028, the strategy is intended to deliver more coordinated border management, stronger action against trafficking and smuggling, improved reintegration support and more reliable migration data.

gh.headline: Ghana Tourism Society sets three-day youth festival at Legon
gh.dek: The November 19-21 event will combine tourism education, a fair and cultural performances as the society marks its 20th anniversary.
paragraphs: The Tourism Society of Ghana and the University of Ghana will host the 2026 Youth in Tourism Festival from Thursday, November 19, to Saturday, November 21, at the university’s VIP Car Park in Accra. The organisers say the festival is intended to encourage young people to explore domestic tourism and preserve Ghanaian culture.

The programme includes a Tourism Summit, a campus tour featuring the Visit Ghana double-decker bus, a tourism fair and exhibition, Bajoo Night and a health walk. The summit is due to bring students, academics and tourism professionals together to discuss entrepreneurship, cultural preservation, destination marketing and careers in the sector.

The festival coincides with the Tourism Society of Ghana’s 20th anniversary. Hotels, travel agencies, tour operators, airlines and other businesses are among the organisations the society has asked to support the event.

cd.headline: Visa RDC launches Android tap-to-pay in Kinshasa
cd.dek: The feature lets users pay at terminals with their phones as the country prepares to ban commercial cash and foreign-currency transactions in April 2027.
paragraphs: Visa RDC launched Tap to Pay on its Visa Pay app in Kinshasa on Monday, enabling users with Android phones to make contactless payments at payment terminals.

Sophie Kafuti, Visa RDC's managing director, said the service lets consumers use a phone as a bank card. The central bank governor, André Wameso, said digital payments are central to the planned reform and to expanding financial inclusion.

The ban on commercial cash and foreign-currency transactions is due to take effect in April 2027. Visa RDC and the central bank said they would run public-awareness activities to encourage people to adopt the payment method.

cd.dek: Fighting between the FRN and the army has worsened insecurity in the South Kivu health zone as cholera spreads and malaria cases peak.
paragraphs: Insecurity following clashes between the FRN and the army is complicating access to health care in Bunyakiri, a health zone in South Kivu, where cholera is spreading and malaria cases have peaked.

The deteriorating security situation is adding to pressure on health services as the two diseases affect the area, Actualite.cd reported on Wednesday. Its report did not provide figures for cases or deaths, or details of steps by health authorities.
The combination of cholera, a malaria surge and insecurity has made the health situation in Bunyakiri more concerning, according to the report.

cd.headline: Congolese youth urged to take a bigger role in peacebuilding
cd.dek: At a Kinshasa conference, organisers asked young people to prevent conflict, back social cohesion and carry their pledges into their communities.
paragraphs: Young Congolese were called on Monday, 16 November, to play a more active role in promoting peace and security in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The appeal came at a conference in Kinshasa organised by Change Your World, the Kinshasa Youth Parliament and the United Nations peacekeeping mission in Congo, MONUSCO, under the theme "Youth in action for peace."

Sarah Tambwe, coordinator of Change Your World, said young people should be placed at the centre of the peace process and given spaces to speak and take part. Youth parliamentarian Jennifer Sarty said young people must not stay on the sidelines of the security challenges facing the country, and urged them to act against violence targeting women and girls.
Organisers asked participants to turn their discussions and pledges into concrete action, and to pass the message on to their peers as awareness leaders.

tz.headline: Samia consults party leaders on commission for constitutional changes
tz.dek: CHADEMA stayed away from the Dar es Salaam meeting, where council members proposed equal representation for both sides of the Union and women.
paragraphs: President Samia Suluhu Hassan met political party leaders at the Dar es Salaam State House on November 16 to discuss forming a Reconciliation and Mediation Commission that would coordinate preparations for constitutional amendments. Tanzania’s main opposition party, CHADEMA, did not attend.

The presidency said members of the Council of Political Parties recommended that the proposed commission represent both sides of the Union and ensure gender equality. The commission has not been established, and its membership and working arrangements have not been announced.

Samia said consultations would continue with political stakeholders, civil institutions and the private sector. In July, CHADEMA deputy chairperson John Heche said the party’s Central Committee required national chairperson Tundu Lissu’s release and a mediator before talks could begin.

tz.headline: TOL Gases lists shares after raising 10.57bn/- in rights issue
tz.dek: The 129 per cent subscription will help fund a carbon dioxide plant and infrastructure expected to cost 15.7bn/-.
paragraphs: TOL Gases PLC began trading newly issued shares on the Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange after a rights issue raised 10.57bn/-, exceeding its 8.17bn/- target. The proceeds are earmarked mainly for a new carbon dioxide plant and supporting infrastructure.

Company chairman Leonard Kitoka said the issue reflected shareholders’ confidence in TOL Gases’ management and growth prospects. Managing director Daniel Warungu said completing the plant by the second quarter of 2027 was the company’s immediate priority; the project is expected to cost 15.7bn/-.

The company expects the plant to increase production capacity and improve supply reliability. The listing brings TOL Gases’ total issued ordinary shares to approximately 69 million, which investors can trade on the secondary market, according to Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange chief business development officer Emmanuel Nyalali.

tz.headline: Tanzania opens Lindi boys’ school under SEQUIP
tz.dek: The school is one of seven regional boys’ secondary schools, easing the need for families in Lindi and Mtwara to send sons far away for education.
paragraphs: Tanzania’s Secondary Education Quality Improvement Project has established seven regional boys’ secondary schools, including Lindi Boys’ Secondary School in the country’s south. The school began classes in July 2026 with 23 Form Five students studying science combinations.

Headmaster Fransico Zebedayo said the school gives families in Lindi and Mtwara a local boarding option, after some had sent children to distant regions for secondary education. He said parents had previously faced the cost of sending their children elsewhere, while such schools had been built exclusively for girls.

The students include 11 taking Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, eight studying Chemistry, Biology and Geography, and four pursuing Physics, Chemistry and Biology. Form Five student Raheem Kondo said boarding allows students to spend more time studying and have teachers available for closer supervision.

tz.headline: NBC launches campaign with TSh 4 million grand prizes for digital payments
tz.dek: The three-month programme runs through February 16, 2027, and includes rewards for customers and 150 merchant cashiers.
paragraphs: National Bank of Commerce (NBC) launched the second edition of its Tabasamu Tukupe Mashavu campaign in Dar es Salaam, with the programme running from November 17, 2026, to February 16, 2027. The bank is promoting card, mobile and other digital payments during the festive season.

NBC said nine grand-prize winners will each receive TSh 4 million: five will be chosen through card transactions and four through Lipa Kiganjani payments. The campaign also offers weekly and monthly draws, and 150 cashiers using NBC point-of-sale terminals can earn rewards tied to growth in transaction value, Head of Transactions Mangire Kibanda said.

Customers can enter through NBC cards, its Kiganjani mobile service, Lipa Kiganjani, NBC agents and ATMs. The Gaming Board of Tanzania will supervise all prize draws, while customers can open accounts through the Kiganjani app after registration and verification.

tz.headline: Karimjee Foundation and Glasgow mark 10 years of Tanzania conservation scholarships
tz.dek: The programme has supported 25 Tanzanians, and every graduate is now working in conservation in Tanzania, the foundation’s chair said.
paragraphs: The Karimjee Foundation and the University of Glasgow marked 10 years of their conservation scholarship programme at a gathering in Dar es Salaam held over the weekend. The programme funds Tanzanians to take a master’s degree in African Ecosystem Conservation Management at Glasgow.

Foundation chair Yusuf Karimjee said students spend one year studying in Glasgow and a second year on practical training in Tanzania, including a long research project. The foundation covers tuition and living allowances and offers up to two scholarships each year. Karimjee said 25 Tanzanians, past and present, have taken part, and every graduate now works in conservation in Tanzania.

Karimjee said 11 participants have gone on to PhD studies, while the group has published 16 scientific papers and made more than 20 conference presentations. Graduates teach conservation scientists and contribute research used in wildlife management and community safety, he said. He urged alumni, partners and university staff to discuss the programme’s next 10 years.

ma.headline: Morocco plans no-extra-cost roaming across more mobile networks
ma.dek: The government wants operators that are alone in an area to open their networks to other subscribers, with phones switching automatically.
paragraphs: Morocco plans to expand national roaming so mobile subscribers can use another operator’s network at no change in tariff, with phones switching automatically. Digital Transition Minister Ahmed Rahhou announced the plan on Monday in the House of Representatives, answering a question about extending telecom services nationwide.

The service already covers more than 7,000 zones. The ministry plans to require an operator that is the only one covering an area to admit subscribers of rival networks, because some zones cannot economically support all three operators.

The ministry will study satellite coverage for remote “white zones” with telecom regulator ANRT and operators, subject to safety and security requirements. A preliminary survey checked nearly 50,000 kilometres of roads; about 15,700 kilometres of provincial roads remain to be checked. Those checks will continue in 2027, and the ministry wants operators to cover the roads within a year or two at most. A rural internet plan is also expected to reach 2,000 weakly covered or uncovered zones this year.

ma.headline: Morocco and Mauritania move to update 1986 trade pact
ma.dek: The two governments also plan a framework for agricultural and food shipments and an investment forum in Mauritania in early 2027.
paragraphs: Morocco and Mauritania have agreed to work toward updating their trade agreement, signed in August 1986, and to develop joint projects in agriculture, food processing, fisheries and energy. The plans were announced in a joint statement after trade ministers Omar Hejira of Morocco and Zeinebou Mint Ahmednah of Mauritania met in Nouakchott on Tuesday.

The countries will form a working group of trade ministries and relevant sectors to set rules for moving agricultural and food products between them before the end of January 2027. A second session of their Joint Trade Commission is scheduled for Morocco on January 27, 2027, while an investment forum is planned in Mauritania in early 2027.

The forum’s preparations will be led by Morocco’s Agency for the Development of Investments and Exports and Mauritania’s Investment Promotion Agency. The two sides also reached an initial agreement to establish a wholesale market in Nouakchott, with cold storage and slaughterhouses, to improve product marketing and regulate export channels.

ma.headline: Morocco rises to 78th in 2025 climate risk ranking
ma.dek: Germanwatch’s index places the country 18 spots higher than in 2024, while its ranking for the 1996–2025 period fell to 99th.
paragraphs: Morocco ranked 78th among countries affected by extreme weather in 2025, up from 96th in 2024, according to the Climate Risk Index 2027, published by Germanwatch on Tuesday. The report was released during the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye.

The index measures recorded disaster impacts using six indicators, including deaths, people affected and economic losses. Germanwatch said the annual and 30-year rankings measure different periods: Morocco placed 99th for 1996–2025, compared with 83rd in the previous assessment covering 1995–2024.

The rankings do not measure future climate vulnerability, and shifts in position do not necessarily mean losses changed by the same amount. Germanwatch said damage is underreported in developing countries, particularly in Africa, and called for stronger early-warning systems, adaptation investment and international financing.

ma.headline: Waltz backs Morocco’s autonomy plan for Sahara
ma.dek: The U.S. ambassador to the United Nations restated Washington’s position during talks in Rabat with Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita.
paragraphs: Mike Waltz, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, met Morocco’s Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita in Rabat on Tuesday, 17 November, to discuss the Sahara dispute. Bourita reaffirmed Morocco’s commitment to a settlement granting autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty.

Waltz restated Washington’s recognition of Morocco’s sovereignty over the Sahara, according to Maroc Diplomatique. The discussions also covered meetings in Madrid and Washington and the withdrawal of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) observers.

Maroc Diplomatique reported that the mission’s withdrawal had begun the day before. Waltz called on the separatist group to respect the ceasefire and rule out renewed hostilities; the reports gave no further details of the discussions.

ma.headline: AS FAR places four players in CAF Champions League team
ma.dek: The Moroccan club won the 2026 women's title in Egypt and became the first side to retain the trophy, the Confederation of African Football said.
paragraphs: Morocco’s AS FAR placed four players in the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Women’s Champions League 2026 team of the tournament, announced Tuesday. The competition ran from 1 to 15 November in Egypt, where the club secured its third title.

The CAF said the 4-4-2 selection recognised players for their technical performances, consistency and decisive contributions during the tournament. AS FAR was the first club to retain the women’s Champions League title, according to the confederation.

ug.headline: Kampala traders shut shops to protest URA taxes and enforcement
ug.dek: The shutdown closed arcades and commercial buildings as traders called for talks with the Uganda Revenue Authority and a review of business costs.
paragraphs: Traders shut shops across downtown Kampala on Tuesday, 17 November, protesting what they described as excessive taxes and harsh enforcement by the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA). Several arcades and commercial buildings, including Skylight, Dembe and Pentagon arcades, remained closed during the day.

Yusuf Kalungi, chairperson of the Kikubo business hub, said traders chose a peaceful shutdown after written requests for a meeting with URA. He said the closure would continue until the government addressed their concerns. Kampala City Traders Association members are seeking changes to tax policy, enforcement and the cost of doing business.

Trader Robert Kagwa Matovu said taxes and rent were making businesses unsustainable, while another trader, Mathias Bwanika, said earnings largely went to those costs. Traders also want representation in Parliament, Kalungi said. Traffic police, military police and Kampala Capital City Authority enforcement teams patrolled the city centre.

ug.headline: Uganda's GROW project has lent Shs161 billion to women-owned businesses
ug.dek: The World Bank-backed programme has made 10,096 loans, with repayment terms of up to 24 months and interest capped at 10 per cent a year.
paragraphs: Uganda's Generating Growth Opportunities and Productivity for Women Enterprises (GROW) Project had recorded 10,096 loans with cumulative disbursements of about Shs161 billion as of June 30, 2026, according to project coordinator Dr Aisha Ruth Biyinzika Kasolo. The project is run by the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development with the Private Sector Foundation Uganda.

Eligible micro and small enterprises must be at least 51 per cent women-owned. Loans range from Shs2 million to Shs200 million, with a minimum of Shs1 million for refugee entrepreneurs, and are repayable over up to 24 months at an annual interest rate capped at 10 per cent. 14 participating financial institutions, including the cooperative lenders UGAFODE, Opportunity Bank and EBO Bank, handle the lending.

Kasolo said credit is paired with business-development services, technical assistance, mentorship, networking and market linkages. The facility covers agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, construction, science and technology, hospitality, creative arts and ICT.

ug.headline: Health Ministry schedules 3.3 million-net drive for Kampala and Wakiso
ug.dek: The three-day distribution, set for November 20 to 22, will send 1,168,700 nets to Kampala and 2,000,216 to Wakiso.
paragraphs: Uganda’s Ministry of Health has scheduled its final 2026 mosquito-net distribution phase for Kampala and Wakiso District, with approximately 3.3 million insecticide-treated nets due to be distributed from November 20 to 22. The ministry says the campaign targets vulnerable people, particularly children under five and pregnant women.

Kampala is allocated 1,168,700 nets for an estimated two million residents, while Wakiso will receive 2,000,216 for about 3.9 million people. The distribution will run through 32 operational units aligned with administrative divisions and municipalities, with access prioritised for low-income urban communities. Acting malaria control programme head Dr Richard Kabanda said Uganda recorded more than 11.7 million malaria cases in 2025 and over 2,300 deaths; more than half of those who died were children under five.

Kabanda said consistent, proper net use can cut malaria transmission by about 50 per cent and reduce childhood mortality by up to 25 per cent. The Kampala-Wakiso phase follows the distribution of more than 17 million nets across several sub-regions since January. The ministry advises recipients to hang new nets for 24 hours before use and seek medical care promptly for malaria symptoms.

ug.headline: Savanna Fibre targets 1 million more homes across East Africa in 2027
ug.dek: The rollout follows 250,000 active subscribers in Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya and would take the company's network past 2 million homes.
paragraphs: Savanna Fibre plans to extend its network to 1 million additional homes across Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya in 2027, after passing 250,000 active subscribers across the three countries. The company announced the target in Cape Town on Monday, ahead of the Africa Tech Festival.

Savanna Telecom (Africa) Limited, the Mauritius-based parent company, said engineering designs are complete and construction will run evenly over 12 months. Once built, the new home passes, meaning homes within reach of the network, will take its footprint from slightly more than 1 million to past 2 million. A sizeable portion will serve towns and suburbs where no operator has laid fibre before.

Savanna says it holds 56% of Uganda's fibre-to-the-home market but has not disclosed how many of its subscribers are in the country. Across the nation, the Uganda Communications Commission logged roughly 196,000 active fixed internet subscriptions in the third quarter of 2025. The 2027 build in Uganda will fall under the commission's optical-fibre installation framework, which took effect on Jan. 1.

ug.headline: Absa Uganda completes Standard Chartered retail and wealth banking acquisition
ug.dek: The transfer brings 162 former Standard Chartered employees to Absa, and migrated customers keep their existing products and services.
paragraphs: Absa Bank Uganda has completed its acquisition of Standard Chartered Bank Uganda’s wealth and retail banking business, a deal first announced in October 2025. The transfer expands Absa’s personal, affluent wealth and business banking operations in Uganda.

The bank said 162 former Standard Chartered employees have joined Absa. Customers have moved to Absa while retaining their existing products and services, and can use its digital platforms, branches and ATMs. Absa will assist customers with account access, digital registration, cards and other service enquiries.

Absa Managing Director David Wandera said the bank would combine the two institutions’ expertise in relationship management, financial advice and personalised banking. The expanded offer includes transactional banking, savings, lending and investment services; Absa also says it has upgraded its digital platforms and introduced Absa Investments, an investment and advisory service.

zw.headline: Zimbabwe miners challenge RBZ over 30% foreign-currency surrender
zw.dek: The dispute pits mining companies seeking greater access to foreign currency against the central bank’s exporter-retention system.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe’s mining industry is pressing the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) for greater access to foreign currency, challenging a system that requires exporters to surrender 30% of their earnings.

Under the policy, exporters retain 70% of foreign-currency earnings and hand the remaining 30% to the central bank. The dispute reflects opposing positions: miners want more access to the currency they earn, while the RBZ is determined to preserve the current arrangement.
The Zimbabwe Independent reported the dispute on 16 November. The account provides no details of a proposed policy change or a next step by either side.

zw.headline: Harare extends settlement regularisation deadline to 31 December
zw.dek: The city says thousands of properties have been recorded as it moves to a second phase focused on infrastructure and land rights.
paragraphs: The City of Harare has extended the Phase 1 deadline for residents, developers and beneficiaries of stands in dysfunctional and illegal settlements to 31 December 2026. Acting Town Clerk Warren Sean Chiwawa announced the extension in a public notice on 17 November, replacing the previous deadline of 17 November.

The council said the extra time followed a large number of people coming forward and requests from residents’ associations, civic organisations and development partners. It reported that thousands of properties had been recorded, accounts created and development compliance assessments carried out.

The city said Phase 2 would begin immediately, shifting from paperwork to physical development in areas that meet regularisation requirements. Planned work includes water and sewer infrastructure, roads and council-supervised planning; the phase also covers land tenure, value and use, with the council seeking to secure recognised ownership and address multiple allocations and land baronism.

zw.headline: Zimbabwe forecasters warn of storms and possible hail through Friday
zw.dek: The Meteorological Services Department expects scattered thunderstorms, strong winds and localised downpours across the country, with the wettest conditions from Sunday to Friday.
paragraphs: Across the country, from Sunday through Friday, the Meteorological Services Department (MSD) has forecast scattered thunderstorms, strong winds and possible hailstorms, with localised downpours at their heaviest.

Harare Metropolitan, Matabeleland North, Manicaland and all Mashonaland provinces face the first wave on 15 and 16 November, and the system then reaches every area from 16 to 20 November, according to an advisory issued with the Department of Civil Protection. The MSD warned of lightning, flash floods in low-lying areas, river basins and urban centres, and winds that can damage crops, roofs and structures.

People are told to shelter indoors during lightning, avoid sailing in storms and postpone trips where possible. Households are urged to secure loose items, repair rooftops and keep away from windows and glass doors.

zw.headline: Former Highlanders vice-chairman survives two road accidents in four days
zw.dek: Modern Ngwenya escaped injury in both crashes, including one near Kwekwe while he was travelling to Harare on Monday morning.
paragraphs: Modern Ngwenya, a former vice-chairman of Zimbabwe’s Highlanders Football Club, survived two road accidents within four days, escaping physical injury in both. The first happened on Thursday on the Gweru-Bulawayo Road as he and veteran journalist Ezra “Tshisa” Sibanda returned from Lower Gweru; their vehicle hit a stray animal.

On Monday morning, about 30 km outside Kwekwe, Ngwenya was driving to Harare when he swerved to avoid an oncoming vehicle and lost control, Sibanda said in a Facebook post. The car left the road, returned to the highway and veered off again, hitting small trees before stopping about 50 metres from where Ngwenya first lost control. He was travelling at about 100 km/h.

Sibanda said Ngwenya was shaken and traumatised, and expressed relief that he had survived both crashes. The incidents come amid deaths in the Highlanders community this year, including four club figures killed in a July road accident and six supporters killed in August.

cv.headline: Cape Verde government pays overdue carnival grants to São Vicente groups
cv.dek: Each group receives two million escudos, the overdue amount plus an advance on the December instalment.
paragraphs: Cape Verde's government has transferred two million escudos to each official carnival group in São Vicente, doubling the grant, Culture Minister António Sequeira Duarte said. The payment covers an overdue tranche and an advance on the instalment originally due in December.

Duarte said the delay came from circumstances and processing at the Finance Ministry, and that the problem has now been resolved. He said support also reaches carnival festivities in other municipalities, but the national total for the 2027 carnival is not yet available.

Support for the remaining municipalities will be arranged between December and early January with association leaders and municipal councils. Separately, São Vicente's municipal council deposited 1,000 contos for each group ahead of the 2027 contest, scheduled for 9 February.

paragraphs: The Banco de Cabo Verde has opened national public tender No. 10/2026 to hire a specialist company to maintain its data-centre infrastructure and the three-phase uninterruptible power supply (UPS) at the bank’s headquarters in Praia, Santiago.

cv.headline: Cape Verde records 372 prostate cancer cases over three years
cv.dek: Carla Barbosa said diagnoses rose most between 2024 and 2025, but better detection and cancer registration may explain part of the increase.
paragraphs: Cape Verde recorded 372 prostate cancer cases over three years, Carla Barbosa of the national programme for cancer prevention and control said at a men’s health workshop. Diagnoses rose most between 2024 and 2025, she said, but the increase does not necessarily mean the disease became more common.

The cancer registry shows the most diagnoses among men aged 50 to 79. Barbosa said 50 people died from prostate cancer in 2022, making it the cancer that contributed most to cancer deaths in the country. She said late detection contributes to mortality, while early diagnosis is associated with better treatment and survival prospects.

Barbosa cited limited access to diagnostic tests across the islands, shortages of specialists and the absence of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging and PET scanning in the public system. She also said Cape Verde lacks radiotherapy and called for stronger imaging and pathology services, decentralised care and closer links between health centres and hospitals.

cv.headline: Lula meets Neves in Praia to discuss new Brazil-Cape Verde cooperation
cv.dek: Brazil's president congratulated Neves on his re-election and discussed cooperation in digital transformation, energy, agriculture and health.
paragraphs: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met Cape Verdean President José Maria Neves in Praia on Monday, 16 November, during a technical stop on his return from COP31 in Turkey. Lula congratulated Neves, who had been re-elected on Sunday, 15 November, for a second presidential term.

The meeting took place in the VIP room at Nelson Mandela International Airport, with Cape Verde's foreign affairs and communities minister, Manuel Amante da Rosa, also present. The two presidents discussed expanding bilateral ties and said they wanted to advance new cooperation initiatives soon.

They identified digital transformation, the energy transition, agriculture, agro-food industry and health as priority areas. Education, higher education and science were also discussed as established fields of cooperation between the two countries.

td.headline: Chad bans shops and stalls in and around schools
td.dek: Prime Minister Allah-Maye Halina’s circular also bars telecoms pylons, advertising signs and non-school events at public and private schools.
paragraphs: Chad’s Prime Minister, Amb. Allah-Maye Halina, signed a circular on 16 November 2026 banning commercial and non-school activities inside and around public and private schools. It prohibits street stalls, kiosks, shops and mobile vendors, as well as bars and drinking venues.

The circular also bars telecommunications pylons and advertising signs, gambling and card-playing spaces, and livestock raising unless it is part of an approved educational project. Halina said unauthorised installations threaten pupils’ physical safety and disrupt lessons.

Administrative, municipal and education authorities are to survey irregular installations, carry out necessary clearances and keep school grounds free of them. The circular also calls for regular monitoring, citing a 4 November 2024 law on the division of powers.

td.headline: African Union education centre reviews girls’ schooling in N’Djamena
td.dek: The delegation examined school re-entry measures, programmes for girls out of school and the results of the #AfricaEducatesHer campaign during a 11-13 November mission.
paragraphs: A delegation from the African Union International Centre for the Education of Girls and Women in Africa completed an evaluation mission in N’Djamena, Chad, from 11 to 13 November 2026. It reviewed the situation of girls’ education and the implementation of the continental #AfricaEducatesHer campaign.

Led by programme officer Boubakar Yougbare, the team met Chad’s education officials and visited schools, a girls’ vocational training centre and a centre for survivors of gender-based violence. The delegation also examined school re-entry arrangements and programmes for girls who are not enrolled, while authorities outlined ongoing initiatives and progress.

The mission included discussions with international organisations and civil-society groups. The centre said the visit was supported by the World Bank through the East Africa Girls’ Empowerment and Resilience project; the delegation also identified mothers’ education associations, hygiene kits and listening centres among practices in use.

paragraphs: Chadian professor Foumsou Lhagadang was elected secretary-general of the Conference of Deans of French-Speaking African Medical Faculties in Bangui, Central African Republic. The election process involved 19 countries.

Lhagadang is dean of the Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of N’Djamena and heads obstetrics at the Mother and Child University Hospital. The conference brings together deans of French-speaking medical faculties, with cooperation focused in part on training and medical education.

dj.headline: Djibouti secures direct Hajj flights and medical care for 2027 pilgrims
dj.dek: Agreements with Saudi providers also cover lodging, meals and ground transport in Mecca and Medina, plus airport help for older and less mobile travellers.
paragraphs: Djibouti’s delegation has signed three agreements for the 2027 Hajj, covering ground services, medical care and direct flights to Medina and Jeddah. The contracts follow a memorandum on the season signed by Djibouti’s minister and Saudi Hajj Minister Tawfiq Al-Rabiah.

Saudi company Al Rifadah will provide lodging in Mecca and Medina, meals, ground transport and reception at Mina, Arafat and Muzdalifa. Al Abeer Medical Group will offer round-the-clock emergency consultations, specialist care, tests, imaging, hospital treatment and medicines through facilities in Mecca’s Al Aziziyah district and Medina. Care will be coordinated with Djibouti’s medical mission, with older people and those with chronic illnesses prioritised.

Saudi airline Flynas has agreed to direct flights to Medina and Jeddah at preferred times, simplified check-in and checked-baggage handling for five-litre Zamzam water containers. It also agreed to assist older passengers and people with reduced mobility at airports and on board.

dj.headline: Djibouti recommends four more coaching days for 24 farm cooperatives
dj.dek: A review of the pilot backed by the International Finance Corporation proposes extra coaching, stronger trainer preparation and new teaching materials.
paragraphs: Djibouti’s agriculture value-chain project unit hosted a review of the Agricultural Leadership Programme, backed by the International Finance Corporation, the World Bank’s private-sector arm. The programme’s pilot covered 24 cooperatives across the country.

The review mission recommended extending the pilot, with four additional days of coaching for each cooperative, more training for trainers and new learning materials. Abdoulkader Issé, the programme’s focal point at the project unit, said the programme was intended to strengthen cooperatives and their economic weight.

Participants discussed which institution would lead the programme and how responsibilities and coordination would be organised. A second phase could start in early March 2027; they also raised a national study of cooperatives and the programme’s links to legal reforms underway.

sz.headline: Eswatini inflation rises to 3.4 per cent ahead of CBE meeting
sz.dek: Annual inflation climbed from 2.9 per cent in September, ahead of the Central Bank's final Monetary Policy Consultative Committee meeting on Friday.
paragraphs: Eswatini's annual inflation rose to 3.4 per cent in October, up from 2.9 per cent in September, just before the Central Bank's final Monetary Policy Consultative Committee meeting on Friday.

Month on month, prices rose 0.9 per cent, according to the October Consumer Price Index report from the Central Statistical Office, faster than the 0.2 per cent recorded the month before. Housing and utilities, along with transport, together added 3.0 percentage points to the headline rate.

In September the bank lifted its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 7.0 per cent, which pushed the prime lending rate to 10.25 per cent. Policymakers will weigh the direction of rates at the Friday meeting.

sz.headline: Eswatini brings in 104 grass bales for livestock farmers
sz.dek: The National Agricultural Marketing Board bought the feed in South Africa as farmers prepare for an anticipated El Niño drought.
paragraphs: Eswatini has received 104 grass bales from South Africa to provide feed for livestock farmers ahead of an anticipated El Niño drought. The National Agricultural Marketing Board (NAMBOARD) procured the batch for the Ministry of Agriculture.

Agriculture Minister Mandla Tshawuka said the bales are the first part of a larger order of thousands secured in South Africa to support the national herd. He urged livestock farmers to form groups and buy feed collectively to make it more accessible and cost-effective.

The Food and Agriculture Organization has provided E5 million for agricultural interventions to mitigate the dry spell. Tshawuka also urged crop farmers in areas that have received early rains to start planting while moisture is available.

sz.headline: UNDP to run E508.5 million climate programme across three countries
sz.dek: The Adaptation Fund approved the regional funding for projects in Eswatini, Zambia and Zimbabwe, with work scheduled from 2027 to 2032.
paragraphs: Eswatini will share a E508.5 million (US$30 million) climate adaptation programme with Zambia and Zimbabwe, to be implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) from 2027 to 2032. The Adaptation Fund approved the regional initiative in April 2026.

The programme will finance locally designed catchment projects to improve water security, restore damaged ecosystems and protect agricultural livelihoods. Smallholder farmers and herders are among its intended beneficiaries as Eswatini faces an El Niño-related drought threat in the 2026/2027 agricultural season, with below-normal rainfall and higher temperatures expected to pressure crops, livestock and water supplies.

Eswatini’s Ministry of Tourism and Environmental Affairs is the country’s executing entity. The programme will also explore payment for ecosystem services and partnerships with national banks to help fund climate-resilient agriculture. UNDP said droughts in 2015/2016 and 2023/2024 affected about 40 million and 60 million people across Southern Africa, respectively.

sz.headline: Dlamini says South Africa athletics reform is on track to avoid suspension
sz.dek: The World Athletics-appointed reform overseer says a new constitution is due for ratification on November 28 before submission to the global body.
paragraphs: Athletics Eswatini President Zakhele Dlamini said South Africa’s athletics federation is on course to avoid international suspension after a two-day reform meeting with its board in Kempton Park, Johannesburg, at the weekend. Dlamini is the World Athletics representative overseeing governance changes at Athletics South Africa (ASA).

Dlamini said ASA remains in good standing with World Athletics and is not suspended. The talks produced a roadmap for a new constitution, which is scheduled for ratification at an ASA Council Meeting on November 28, 2026, before submission to World Athletics ahead of fresh elections.

South Africa’s acting sports minister, Gayton McKenzie, and the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee backed the process. The confederation seconded Jacques Faul and Nomsa Mahlangu to Dlamini’s task force. ASA Acting President Jean Verster said the overhaul is intended to protect athletes from missing World Athletics deadlines.

ga.headline: SEEG repairs 20 kV cable after outages in Libreville and Akanda
ga.dek: The underground line serving several neighbourhoods failed on 15 November; the cable had been in service for more than 28 years.
paragraphs: A fault in a 20 kV underground cable cut electricity to several neighbourhoods in Libreville and Akanda from about 3:45 a.m. on Sunday, 15 November. The Société d’énergie et d’eau du Gabon (SEEG), Gabon’s electricity and water company, traced the failure to the Gué-Gué feeder near the Charbonnages interchange.

SEEG said the cable had been installed more than 28 years ago. Its repair teams located the fault and began work, which requires digging to reach the damaged section. Heavy road traffic in the area is making access and repairs more difficult, the company said.

The affected areas include Tri Postal Charbonnage, École Bas de Gué-Gué, Mairie Haut de Gué-Gué and Cité Kalikac. SEEG had announced that power would be restored on Monday afternoon, 16 November, and said its teams remained at work.

ga.headline: Kossy consults farmers and entrepreneurs on Gabon's 2026-2030 food plan
ga.dek: The agriculture minister heard calls on land, finance, training and market access as he seeks input for the national strategy.
paragraphs: Gabon’s agriculture minister, Pacôme Kossy, met agricultural professional organisations, women and young entrepreneurs in Libreville on 16 November to gather proposals for the 2026-2030 Food Systems Transformation Plan (PTSA).

Participants raised barriers to agricultural enterprise, including access to land and finance, training, competitiveness, certification and marketing local produce. Kossy presented planned support mechanisms and asked them to submit recommendations, according to Gabon Review.

Consultations were due to continue on 18 November at the Palais des Congrès Omar-Bongo-Ondimba in the Cité de la démocratie. The plan is intended to modernise production, organise value chains, attract investment and create jobs, while reducing reliance on food imports and expanding local processing by 2030.

ga.headline: Eurofinsa seeks freeze on Gabon’s Bank of New York Mellon funds
ga.dek: The Spanish contractor wants access to nearly 18 million dollars tied to Libreville’s unfinished Omar-Bongo stadium project.
paragraphs: Eurofinsa asked a federal judge in New York on 12 November 2026 to stop Gabon from transferring public funds held at the Bank of New York Mellon. The Spanish construction group is seeking payment of an arbitration award over the stalled rehabilitation of Libreville’s Omar-Bongo stadium.

A federal judge in Washington ordered Gabon to pay 17 898 152,10 dollars on 17 January 2025, after the country did not respond to Eurofinsa’s enforcement case. The award followed a 15 October 2020 arbitration ruling requiring Gabon to pay more than 12 million euros, with annual interest of 3,66%; Eurofinsa’s 437 400 euros owed to the state was deducted.

Eurofinsa, which Madrid’s Commercial Court No. 17 declared bankrupt in January 2023 with liabilities of 306 million euros, is pursuing the funds through its court-appointed administrator, Baker Tilly. The dispute began with a 2009 stadium contract; the stadium’s rehabilitation remains unfinished.

gm.headline: Barrow leads CepRass poll with 37.9% before Gambia election
gm.dek: The survey found 52% dissatisfied with government delivery on promises and 80% rating the national economy badly.
paragraphs: Among respondents holding valid voter cards, 37.9% said they would back the incumbent, according to a survey by the Centre for Policy, Research and Strategic Studies (CepRass). The Gambia’s presidential election is scheduled for December 5.

United Democratic Party leader Ousainou A.N.M. Darboe received 24.2% and Talib Ahmed Bensouda 11.3%. 52 percent of respondents judged the government’s delivery on promises ineffective or very ineffective, 80% rated the national economy badly, and 43% named the cost of living as the country’s biggest concern.

Fieldwork ran from October 17 to November 1, with 1,180 people questioned in 118 enumeration areas across all eight local government areas. CepRass said the figures capture opinion during fieldwork and should not be read as a forecast of the result. Candidate competence was the leading stated influence on voting decisions, cited by 39%.

gm.headline: ActionAid urges peaceful campaigning ahead of Gambia’s Dec. 5 vote
gm.dek: The non-partisan group called on candidates, parties and supporters to obey electoral laws and keep political competition free of intimidation and violence.
paragraphs: ActionAid International The Gambia has urged political parties, presidential candidates, supporters and the public to campaign peacefully and follow electoral laws as campaigning begins for the Dec. 5, 2026, presidential election. In a statement issued Monday, the non-partisan organisation said political competition must respect peace and tolerance.

The organisation called on party leaders and candidates to honour the Peace Pact they signed through their conduct during the campaign, on election day and after results are announced. It urged the Independent Electoral Commission to act independently and fairly, and security agencies to protect citizens and electoral participants while exercising restraint.

ActionAid also asked citizens, media and social media users to respect differing views and verify information before sharing it. It said voters must be able to cast ballots without intimidation, while electoral complaints should be resolved through legal and institutional processes.

gm.headline: Bensouda pledges Banjul-Barra bridge before 2036 if elected
gm.dek: The Coalition 2026 presidential candidate says the link would strengthen trade and help make the North Bank Region The Gambia's commercial capital.
paragraphs: Talib Ahmed Bensouda, the presidential candidate of Coalition 2026, has pledged to build a bridge linking Banjul and Barra before 2036 if elected. He made the promise at spot meetings in Essau and Pakau Njoku and at a rally in Munyagen, in Jokadou.

Bensouda said the North Bank could become The Gambia's commercial capital, given its location near Senegal and regional cities such as Dakar and Bamako. He said the bridge is a key commitment in his coalition's manifesto and that without such a link the region would struggle to reach its full economic potential.

He said the bridge was something the government under President Barrow could not deliver. "Within 10 years, we will bridge Banjul and Barra," Bensouda said. "Before 2036, there will be a Banjul-Barra Bridge."

gm.headline: Germany equips Gambian hospital's children's emergency unit with heart scanner
gm.dek: The German Embassy also paid for five days of echocardiography training for resident doctors at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital.
paragraphs: The German Embassy in The Gambia has donated an echography machine to the Emergency Paediatric Unit at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital (EFSTH) to help doctors diagnose congenital heart defects in children on time. The embassy also sponsored a five-day echocardiography course for selected resident doctors so they can operate the machine.

Dr. Sara Loetz, head of the unit, said children make up about 40% of The Gambia's population and that the neonatal unit alone had more than 135 babies in far too little space last week. She said about 1% of babies worldwide are born with congenital heart conditions. Professor Augusta Eneh, head of the hospital's paediatric department, said the country's ability to diagnose these defects quickly had been limited by a lack of diagnostic tools and specialised training.

Dr. Cherno Jallow, deputy chief medical director at EFSTH, said the embassy had gone beyond giving a machine by building staff capacity to use it. German Envoy Klaus Botzet said machines do not work by themselves and depend on trained people.

gm.headline: Gambia lets 2-1 lead slip to draw with Ivory Coast
gm.dek: Musa Barrow scored a 79th-minute penalty, but Ivory Coast equalised with the final kick after Musa Badamosi was sent off.
paragraphs: The Gambia drew 2-2 with Ivory Coast at Independence Stadium after surrendering a 2-1 lead in the closing minutes. Yankuba Minteh equalised in the 68th minute, and Musa Barrow converted a penalty in the 79th to put the Scorpions ahead.

Musa Badamosi was shown a red card after a late confrontation, leaving The Gambia with 10 players. Coach Jonathan McKinstry said the team had lost its discipline, and said Ivory Coast scored with the final kick of the match after stoppage time stretched toward nine minutes.

McKinstry said he would review video of the incident that led to Badamosi’s dismissal, while declining to use the decision as an excuse. He said The Gambia had played well enough to earn the lead but gave it away through a collective failure of discipline.

gn.headline: CBG outlines alumina refinery plan at Conakry mining summit
gn.dek: The Guinean bauxite producer said construction work has begun and it expects to invite guests to a possible opening three years from next year.
paragraphs: Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée (CBG), a Guinean bauxite producer, presented its industrial plans at the first Simandou Mining Summit, held in Conakry from 11 to 14 November 2026. Chief Executive Karifa Condé said the company had started work on an alumina refinery and anticipated an opening in three years, counting from next year.

Condé made the remarks at the summit’s opening ceremony on Kassa Island. CBG’s refinery project is intended to process bauxite in Guinea and add value locally, according to the company. The summit brought together public officials, investors, mining operators and technical partners to discuss local processing, responsible production and community relations.

CBG also described its voluntary adoption of the Aluminium Stewardship Initiative’s performance standard. Pierre Dominique Traoré, the company’s group director for strategy, development and quality, said the standard addresses environmental, social and governance requirements across the aluminium value chain, from bauxite extraction to processing.

gn.headline: Doumbouya appoints senior officials to Guinea’s labour ministry
gn.dek: A decree read on national television on 17 November names officials for employment, workplace safety and labour-market agencies.
paragraphs: Guinean President Mamadi Doumbouya appointed senior officials to the Ministry of Employment, Labour and Social Protection in a decree read on national television on 17 November 2026.

The appointments include Moustapha Diané as secretary-general and Aminata Kouyaté as principal adviser. Elhadj Mamadou Diallo was named director-general of the Guinean Agency for the Promotion of Employment and Entrepreneurship, while Alhousseine Yansané was appointed director-general of the workplace safety and health directorate.

The decree also names leaders for the National Labour Market Observatory and the National Directorate of Labour and Social Welfare. The announcement lists officials’ roles but gives no further details about their plans.

gn.headline: Soutra Money earns top-tier payment security certification
gn.dek: The Guinean fintech says its PCI DSS level 1 status follows a full audit and requires annual reviews of its payment systems and data safeguards.
paragraphs: Soutra Money, a Guinean digital financial services platform, said on 17 September it had earned level 1 certification under the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS), the highest tier of the payment-data security framework. The company is based in Conakry.

The standard applies to organisations that store, process or transmit payment data. Level 1 requires an annual full audit of system security, data protection, access management, continuous monitoring and regular penetration tests, according to the announcement.

Soutra Money said the certification can serve as a prerequisite for large-scale payment-service integrations with commercial, financial and technology partners. It described Guinea’s digital payments market as growing, with security becoming a factor for consumers, merchants, companies and banks.

gn.headline: Guinean commentator urges Burkina Faso to address its own crises
gn.dek: Amadou Tidiane Bah says Burkina Faso’s security and humanitarian challenges should command attention amid media criticism of Guinea.
paragraphs: Amadou Tidiane Bah, a commentator writing in Guinea, has criticised coverage of the country on Burkina Faso’s public broadcaster RTB and urged Ouagadougou to focus on its own security and humanitarian challenges. In an opinion piece published by Mosaiqueguinee, he said some broadcasts and media commentary had portrayed Guinea in a tendentious, caricatured way.

Bah said accusations about Guinea should be documented and verified, and argued that the country has the right to set its public policies and govern its mineral resources under its laws. He also said no clandestine network should replace the Guinean state’s authority on its territory.

He said Burkina Faso faces challenges in protecting its population, controlling territory and restoring stability. Bah added that Guinea remains committed to cooperation with peoples in the subregion, including Burkinabè people, while insisting that this should not be treated as disrespect for its institutions.

gn.headline: Guinea beats Botswana 7-0 to reach final qualifying round
gn.dek: The under-23 side advances to the last round of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after a 1-0 first-leg win.
paragraphs: Guinea’s under-23 team beat Botswana 7-0 at Conakry’s 28-Septembre Stadium on Tuesday, 17 November, to advance from the first round of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. Guinea had won the first leg 1-0.

Botswana’s goalkeeper was sent off in the 17th minute after striking a Guinean player outside the penalty area, leaving the visitors with 10 players. Abdoulaye Kolev Camara opened the scoring in the 23rd minute; Mohamed Kolev Camara added a second before half-time. Abdoul Karim Camara, Aboubacar Bah and Mohamed Bangoura scored between the 50th and 56th minutes, with Bah and Bangoura adding two more late goals.
Guinea will face the Republic of the Congo in the final qualifying round for a place at the tournament. Coach Morlaye Cissé’s team needed only a draw to progress after its first-leg victory.

lr.headline: Liberia House committee urges rejection of OeSD ID concession
lr.dek: The lawmakers cite more than 40 alleged legal, procurement, financial and national-security defects in the proposed civil registry deal.
paragraphs: A joint committee of Liberia’s House of Representatives has urged lawmakers to reject a proposed concession with OeSD International GmbH to develop and manage the country’s central digital civil registry and vital statistics system. The committee identified more than 40 alleged legal, procurement, financial and national-security deficiencies.

In a report submitted to the House Plenary, the committee said the government failed to follow procurement directions for open international bidding and delegated too much authority to the private company. It recommended rejecting the agreement in full and directing the executive branch to address statutory breaches before considering another arrangement.

lr.headline: COP31 draft sets $120 billion adaptation finance target for 2035
lr.dek: The proposed agreement also sets a 35 percent electricity target, while Liberia presses for predictable support and has undisbursed climate commitments.
paragraphs: A draft political agreement at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, proposes annual adaptation finance of US$120 billion for developing countries by 2035. Released by the COP31 presidency on November 16, the text also proposes that electricity make up 35 percent of final energy use by 2035.

The draft calls on developed countries to keep their finance promise, but competing wording on fossil fuels and other issues means it is not an agreed position. Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, chair of the African Group of Negotiators, said African countries want commitments adequately funded, transparently tracked and delivered on fair terms.

Liberia is seeking predictable climate finance and adaptation support, while about US$360 million committed under its previous climate plan remained undisbursed as of December 2024. Civil society groups questioned whether the draft would help secure funding or distract from detailed negotiations needed to deliver it.

lr.headline: Liberia police reopen 2017 cheque complaint against Musa Hassan Bility
lr.dek: The opposition leader says his company’s cheque was never presented for payment and that the debt to former Nigerian partners was settled.
paragraphs: Liberia’s police are examining a 2017 complaint against opposition leader Musa Hassan Bility over a cheque issued by his company, Srimex Oil & Gas Company, to former Nigerian business partners. Bility was called in by Inspector General of Police Gregory O. W. Coleman in July 2026 for further discussions, according to a letter Bility sent Coleman on September 30.

Bility wrote that he understood the matter had been dealt with in 2017 and said the cheque was never presented to Guaranty Trust Bank for payment. He said the underlying obligation had been satisfied. Coleman told him that the police had received written confirmation from Global Bank Liberia, now Bloom Bank Africa Liberia, that the cheque was presented and returned unpaid.

A source familiar with the investigation told FrontPage Africa that Interpol contacted the Liberia National Police about the case. The source said a report was being sent to Justice Minister Bettie Lamin-Blamo but had not been made public. The police have not publicly explained what Interpol requested.

lr.headline: Liberian clinician urges response to estimated 56,000 HIV cases
lr.dek: Patience Lincoln says weak coordination and breaches of patient confidentiality are undermining prevention and treatment across Liberia.
paragraphs: Patience Lincoln, a graduating public health student at the University of Liberia, urged Liberia’s government to strengthen its response to HIV, citing a 2026 estimate of about 56,000 people living with the virus. She described the situation as a national public health emergency.

Lincoln said poor coordination among the Ministry of Health, the National Public Health Institute of Liberia and the National AIDS Commission had weakened efforts to curb transmission. She also alleged that some health workers disclosed patients’ HIV status to relatives and acquaintances, exposing them to discrimination and social rejection.

She said fear of stigma discourages some people from seeking care and following treatment. Lincoln called for stricter enforcement of confidentiality rules, more public awareness, increased budget support and expanded prevention and treatment programmes; she also urged health authorities to improve professional ethics and coordination.

lr.headline: Liberia schedules maritime security dialogue in Margibi County
lr.dek: The Liberia Maritime Authority will convene officials and shipping leaders on Thursday, before the country assumes the UN Security Council presidency in December.
paragraphs: Liberia will host a maritime safety and security dialogue on Thursday, November 19, at the Liberia Maritime Training Institute in Marshall, Margibi County. The Liberia Maritime Authority (LiMA) scheduled the meeting for 10 a.m., as the country prepares to assume the rotating presidency of the United Nations Security Council in December 2026.

LiMA Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer Neto Zarzar Lighe announced the event at a Ministry of Information briefing on November 17. He said senior government officials, diplomats, United Nations representatives, security experts and shipping industry leaders would discuss threats including piracy, armed conflict, cyberattacks, illegal fishing and trafficking.

The talks are set to cover international shipping routes, seafarer protection, information sharing and coordination. Lighe said Liberia, one of the world’s leading flag states, has a responsibility to promote maritime safety, freedom of navigation and cooperation.

ly.headline: Libyan government warns it will reorganise regional administration after Zintan session...
ly.dek: The government says it will act if obstruction of the House of Representatives continues, giving regions more authority over their administration, finances and public resources.
paragraphs: Libya's government warned on Monday, November 16, that it will take urgent administrative and financial measures in areas under its control after the House of Representatives failed to hold a formal session in Zintan. The measures could give regions greater autonomy over administration, finances and public resources.

In Statement No. 17 for 2026, issued in Benghazi, the government said threats and attempts to block lawmakers from meeting prevented them from carrying out their constitutional duties. It called the developments dangerous and unacceptable, and said interference with constitutional institutions threatens national unity and stability.

The government thanked the people, elders and leaders of Zintan for preparing to host the session. It said it remains committed to ending national division, but that the responsibility cannot be one-sided, and held all parties disrupting state institutions accountable for any consequences.

ly.headline: Libya's central bank governor urges a unified national budget
ly.dek: Fawzi Abu Khazam told Finance Minister Rashid Abu Ghaffa that a single budget would consolidate public spending and strengthen fiscal discipline.
paragraphs: Central Bank of Libya Governor Fawzi Abu Khazam urged adoption of a unified national budget in a meeting with Finance Minister Rashid Abu Ghaffa in Tripoli. The two discussed joint technical arrangements and ways to strengthen cooperation between the central bank and the ministry.

Abu Khazam said a single budget was needed to consolidate public spending and improve fiscal discipline. He also stressed the bank's independence and said it would coordinate with state institutions within existing laws.

The governor called for a firm commitment to combating money laundering, terrorist financing and corruption, and for essential economic reforms. The bank and the Ministry of Economy and Trade had agreed on 11 November that documentary letters of credit would be issued to applicants on the basis of national priorities identified by the ministry, to ration hard-currency releases and save reserves.

paragraphs: Libya's state medical purchasing entity, the Medical Supply Organisation (MSO), has invited relevant entities and institutions to a two-day Medical Supply Forum for Dialogue and Development in Tripoli on 21 and 22 December.

mg.headline: Madagascar and US sign military logistics accord for maritime patrols
mg.dek: The deal lets both armed forces exchange supplies, services and logistical support for joint patrols, exercises and crisis response.
paragraphs: Madagascar and the United States signed a military acquisition and mutual assistance agreement in Antananarivo on Tuesday, creating a framework for the two armed forces to exchange supplies, services and logistical support. The accord can be used for humanitarian operations, military exercises and crises.

The arrangement also provides mutual support for joint maritime patrols and multinational exercises, including Cutlass Express. US Africa Command deputy operations director General Thomas M. Armas, who signed for the United States, said reliable logistics were needed for operations, including cyclone response and securing waters in the Mozambique Channel. Madagascar’s Armed Forces Minister, General Maminirina Ely Razafitombo, signed for Madagascar.

A roundtable after the signing discussed port infrastructure and bases for refuelling operations in Antsiranana, Toamasina and Mahajanga. 24 Malagasy troops received practical training in procurement, emergency fuel supply and air support. The signing followed a visit by AFRICOM deputy commander General John Brennan two weeks earlier; Madagascar is among more than 30 African partner countries using the agreement.

mg.headline: FAGACE opens Madagascar office to guarantee up to 50% of loans
mg.dek: The fund says its Antananarivo representation will help small and medium-sized businesses secure bank credit by sharing lenders’ risk.
paragraphs: The African Fund for Guarantee and Economic Cooperation (FAGACE) opened a representative office in Madagascar on Monday, 16 November, at Antaninarenina. The fund can guarantee up to 50% of a loan, subject to conditions, according to Madagascar’s central bank, cited by the prime minister’s office.

The guarantee is intended to reduce the risk banks bear when lending to businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises struggling to raise investment funds. Agriculture and renewable energy are among the sectors covered. The prime minister’s office said the fund’s local presence is intended to improve Malagasy businesses’ access to bank credit.

The office’s practical access rules, selection criteria and financing terms have yet to be set out. FAGACE said it intends to provide financial solutions for local businesses, beyond technical support.

mg.headline: Madagascar Airlines critic says leadership change risks its recovery
mg.dek: Former chief executive Thierry de Bailleul says the airline had restored five ATRs to service and reached structural profitability before the funding programme was suspended.
paragraphs: Madagascar Airlines’ former chief executive, Thierry de Bailleul, says the carrier’s recovery was disrupted after authorities ended continuity in its leadership. In an opinion article, he says the Phénix 2030 restructuring plan, backed by the World Bank, had restored five ATR aircraft to operation, compared with one at the start of the effort.

De Bailleul says the airline achieved more than 82% punctuality, increased domestic capacity by 123% compared with 2022 and grew revenue by 60% in two years. He reports structural profitability of +5M$ excluding non-recurring items, and says the World Bank had been preparing 80 M$ in additional financing, including 40 M$ for the airline, subject to conditions including governance.

He says the financing programme was suspended the week after his departure. The former executive argues the carrier should focus on reliable domestic routes, regional services and international partnerships; he warns that operational deterioration observed over the past two months risks a relapse if it continues.

mw.dek: Information Minister Shadric Namalomba says the government expects fuel supplies to improve, but cannot give a date for ending the crisis.

mw.headline: Malawi urges irrigation push ahead of potential Super El Niño
mw.dek: An opinion article says farmers should expand dry-season crops and repair irrigation schemes to build food reserves before extreme weather hits.
paragraphs: A Times Group Malawi opinion article by MacPherson Tadziwa Mdalla urges the government, businesses and farming communities to expand irrigation-based food production ahead of a potential Super El Niño. It proposes winter cropping around Lake Malawi and along major river systems, as well as rehabilitating existing schemes.

Mdalla says Malawi relies heavily on rain-fed agriculture and that droughts, floods and crop failures have left millions vulnerable to food insecurity. Smallholders already grow crops along riverbanks and wetlands in the dry season, but limited access to irrigation equipment, finance, quality inputs and storage constrains their output.

The article calls for farmers to receive seeds, fertiliser, extension services and market access, with the aim of producing food for reserves and supporting household incomes. It also identifies Lake Chilwa, Lake Malombe, the Shire, Songwe and Ruo rivers, and dams and wetlands as water resources that could support irrigation.

mw.headline: Storms strip roofs from Mangochi health centre and school classroom
mw.dek: Strong winds blew off the roofs at Phirilongwe Health Centre and nearby staff houses, and a classroom at Majuni Secondary School has been closed.
paragraphs: Stormy rains and strong winds have torn roofs from Phirilongwe Health Centre and staff houses in Chilipa, Mangochi District, leaving patients and health workers exposed to harsh weather. A classroom at Majuni Secondary School in Namwera was also damaged, disrupting learning.

Bishop Witmos, public relations officer for Mangochi District Council, said the council has begun assessing how badly the health centre and staff houses were hit. No students or teachers were hurt, and the damaged classroom was shut temporarily to avoid risk.

The classroom had lost its roof three days earlier in similar storms, Witmos said. The council is urging residents across the district to stay alert as the rainy season continues, to watch changing conditions and to follow safety guidance from authorities.

ml.headline: Mali hands air force seven aircraft for transport and support
ml.dek: The fleet includes one IL-76, four Mi-8 helicopters and two Mi-24 helicopters, funded from the national budget and acquired with Russia.
paragraphs: Mali handed the armed forces an IL-76 transport plane, four Mi-8 helicopters and two Mi-24 helicopters at Sénou airport on Monday, 16 November. The aircraft are assigned to heavy transport, troop mobility, air support and medical evacuations.

Brigadier General Alou Boï Diarra, head of the air force, said it recorded more than 7 000 sorties and nearly 26 000 flight hours from January to October 2026. It transported about 28 000 passengers and more than 2 000 tonnes of freight during that period.

The government said the aircraft were bought with Russia’s cooperation and paid for from the national budget. It did not publish the purchase cost, contract terms or full delivery schedule. Their regular use will depend on crew availability, maintenance and spare-parts supply.

ml.headline: Mali begins demolitions on 9.3-kilometre Samé road section
ml.dek: The work between the GMS roundabout and Kati clears the route for a four-lane upgrade under a 92.661 billion CFA-franc contract.
paragraphs: Mali began demolishing buildings and installations on Monday, 16 November, along the route from the GMS roundabout through Samé to Kati. The section covers 9.3 kilometres and is planned as a two-by-two-lane road.

The transport and urban-planning ministries announced the operation, which affects families and businesses along the route. The road carries daily travel between Bamako and Kati, freight and local commerce, as well as heavy two-wheel traffic.

The road works, awarded to COVEC-Mali, form part of a wider contract approved in 2024 and valued at 92.661 billion CFA francs including taxes. The project also covers 11.481 kilometres on the Bamako–Koulouba–Kati road, a 1.7-kilometre spur to Point G Hospital and seven kilometres of roads in Kati. The contract period is 36 months.

mr.headline: Mauritania's parliament approves two International Development Association financing deals
mr.dek: The loans fund a social protection overhaul and an extension of high-speed digital infrastructure, and must be repaid over 20 years.
paragraphs: Mauritania's parliament approved two financing agreements with the International Development Association (IDA), the World Bank's concessional lending arm, on Monday. The texts cover the strengthening of resilience and productive social safety nets, and an additional loan for the digital transformation project under the first phase of the regional West African digital integration programme.

Economic Development Minister Mohamedou Ahmedou M'Haimid told deputies that the first agreement, signed on 21 August 2026, will fund technical assistance to review the social registry, its payment system and its complaints procedures. The second, signed on 16 September 2026, is worth €25.8 million and will extend high-speed digital infrastructure, develop digital services and integrate digital markets across West Africa.
The loan is repayable over 20 years, with a five-year grace period, annual interest of 1.5% and a 0.5% annual commitment fee on amounts not yet disbursed.

mr.headline: Mauritania weighs border risks after UN ends MINURSO mandate
mr.dek: The Security Council declined to renew the Western Sahara mission on 30 October, removing a mechanism that monitored incidents and helped contain escalation.
paragraphs: Mauritania is assessing security risks along its northern border after the United Nations Security Council declined to renew the mandate of MINURSO, the UN mission in Western Sahara, on 30 October 2026. The mission’s monitoring role is now ending, removing a mechanism that documented violations, checked incidents and helped contain escalation.

A prospective risk assessment cited by Le Calame rates the chance of armed incidents spilling into Mauritanian territory as low to medium, but their potential impact as very high. It rates risks from weapons and armed groups, and cross-border trafficking, as medium to high in probability and high in impact. The report says northern desert areas could face accidental incursions, gunfire or movements of armed groups.

The report describes continued low-intensity fighting as the more likely of four possible paths, with intermittent clashes and greater uncertainty in Mauritania’s north. A wider escalation could increase pressure on security and civil-protection services; intensified fighting could also displace people toward areas seen as safer, requiring reception, registration, protection and assistance.

mu.headline: Mauritius adopts disaster bill setting work rules for torrential rain
mu.dek: The law bars most employees from being required to work once meteorologists issue a torrential-rain warning and sets higher pay for emergency staff.
paragraphs: Mauritius’ National Assembly adopted the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (Amendment) Bill without changes on Tuesday, 17 November. The law formalises the national protocol for heavy and torrential rain and strengthens protections for workers during severe weather.

Labour Minister Reza Uteem, who sponsored the bill, said it is intended to end differences in how public- and private-sector employees are treated. Once meteorological services issue a torrential-rain warning, employees cannot be required to travel to or remain at work, except emergency-services personnel; the rule does not wait for a National Crisis Committee directive.

During heavy rain, employees are still expected to go to work unless the National Crisis Committee orders or advises them to stay home, shelter or leave. Private-sector emergency staff working on site during torrential rain are entitled to three times their basic hourly rate; those working from home must receive at least twice their usual pay.

mu.headline: Mauritius postpones free school-van project as economic conditions weigh
mu.dek: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam told parliament the plan’s implementation will be reviewed as the economic situation develops.
paragraphs: Mauritius has postponed its planned free school-van service for children, with Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam saying its implementation will be reviewed as the economic situation develops. He announced the delay on Tuesday, 17 November, in response to a question from Rubna Daureeawoo, the MP for Rivière-des-Anguilles/Souillac.

Ramgoolam said the project, included in the Alliance of Change’s election programme, had been delayed because of the economic situation inherited from the previous government. He said ministers recognise the cost school transport places on many parents, while describing school vans as safe transport for young children.

Free transport for students and older people has been in place since 2005 and costs the state Rs 1.6 billion a year, Ramgoolam said; the government will maintain it despite economic constraints. He also said the proposed van service would extend to Rodrigues, which is part of the public transport system.

mu.headline: IPCC recommends criminal charges against four Mauritius police officers
mu.dek: The commission sent its completed investigation into Élodie Thomas’s October shooting to the director of public prosecutions on 17 November.
paragraphs: Mauritius’s Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) has recommended criminal charges against four police officers after investigating the shooting that seriously injured Élodie Thomas, 27, at Camp-Levieux on 9 October. The commission sent its findings to the director of public prosecutions on 17 November.

The IPCC gathered more than 25 statements from police officers, members of the Special Mobile Force and others, and reviewed documents and Safe City camera recordings. Thomas, who left hospital on 6 November, gave her account at home six days later; the commission then held further police interviews from 12 to 16 November.

The investigation began after two complaints were filed on 12 October, one by the driver of the minibus Thomas was travelling in and one on her behalf. Sergeant Gowtamsing Taukoor, arrested on the night of the shooting, faces two provisional charges in court.
